description.en: Crom Cruach (Old Irish: Cromm Crúaich [kɾom ˈkɾuːa̯xʲ]) was a pagan god of pre-Christian Ireland. According to Christian writers, he was propitiated with human sacrifice and his worship was ended by Saint Patrick. He is also referred to as Crom Cróich, Cenn Cruach/Cróich ([kʲen̪ː ˈkɾuːa̯x]) and Cenncroithi ([kʲen̪ː ˈkɾoθʲi]). He is related to the later mythological and folkloric figure Crom Dubh. The references in a dinnsenchas ("place-lore") poem in the 12th century to sacrifice in exchange for milk and grain suggest that Crom had a function as a fertility god. The description of his image as a gold figure surrounded by twelve stone or bronze figures has been interpreted by some as representing the sun surrounded by the signs of the zodiac, suggesting a function as a solar deity.

description.id: Dakini (Dewanagari: डाकिनी; ,IAST: ḍākinī, डाकिनी) adalah sejenis makhluk gaib dalam kepercayaan Hindu dan Buddha. Konsep tentang Dakini berbeda-beda tergantung konteks dan juga tradisi. Sebagai contoh, dalam kitab-kitab Hindu Kuno dan juga naskah Buddhis Tionghoa, istilah tersebut merujuk kepada golongan setan betina yang memangsa daging dan/atau bagian vital manusia. Dalam sastra Tantra Hindu, Dakini adalah nama seorang dewi yang sering dikaitkan dengan salah satu dari enam cakra atau tujuh unsur penting (dhatu) pada tubuh manusia. Dalam kepercayaan Buddhisme di Nepal dan Tibet, dakini dapat mengacu kepada sosok feminin dengan energi tercerahkan berwujud mengerikan, atau wanita yang telah mencapai beberapa tingkatan spiritual, yang kedua-duanya dapat memicu cara-cara Tantra dalam mencapai pencerahan.
description.en: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism. The concept of the dakini somewhat differs depending on the context and the tradition. For example, in earlier Hindu texts and East Asian esoteric Buddhism, the term denotes a race of demonesses who ate the flesh and vital essence of humans. In Hindu Tantric literature, Ḍākinī is the name of a goddess often associated with one of the six chakras or the seven fundamental elements (dhātu) of the human body. Meanwhile, in Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism, dakini (or wisdom dakini) can refer to both what can be best described as fierce-looking female embodiments of enlightened energy, and to human women with a certain amount of spiritual development, both of whom can help Tantric initiates in attaining enlightenment. In Japan, the ḍākinīs – held in the East Asian Buddhist tradition to have been subjugated and converted to Buddhism by the buddha Vairocana under the guise of the god Mahākāla (Daikokuten in Japanese) – were eventually coalesced into a single deity called Dakiniten, who, after becoming syncretized with the native agricultural deity Inari, became linked to the fox (kitsune) iconography associated with the latter.

description.en: Dando's Dogs also known as the Devil's Dandy Dogs, are mythical creatures in English folklore. They are hounds that take part in the Wild Hunt. They are associated with Black Dogs, as a generic term for canine apparitions. The legend involves a sinful priest named Dando, who was a capable huntsman. After a Sunday hunt, Dando drinks all the alcohol that his companions give him. Dando calls for more. He exclaims that if the drink he wants cannot be found on Earth, they should go to Hell to get it. A strange huntsman comes forward and offers Dando a drink, but seizes some of Dando's game from the hunt. A drunken Dando tries to stop the huntsman, shouting, "I'll go to Hell after them, but I'll get them from thee." In another version, a strange huntsman offers Dando a flask. Dando drinks it, but wants more and says that "I'll gallop to Hell for more". In both versions, the huntsman whisks Dando away to Hell, while Dando's dogs give futile chase. It is said that on early Sunday mornings, "Dando's Dogs" can be heard, either pursuing game or searching for Dando.

description.id: Dewa (Dewanagari: देव; ,IAST: Deva, देव) adalah kata dari bahasa Sanskerta yang berarti "terang", "mulia", "makhluk surgawi", "makhluk ilahi", "hal yang cemerlang", dan dapat mengacu kepada suatu golongan makhluk gaib dalam agama Hindu. Dewa merupakan istilah maskulin; padanan feminin untuk istilah tersebut ialah Dewi. Kata tersebut sepadan dengan istilah Latin "Deus" dan Yunani "Zeus". Dalam sastra Weda Kuno, seluruh makhluk gaib dapat disebut "dewa" dan asura. Konsep tersebut akhirnya mengalami perkembangan dalam kesusastraan India Kuno, dan pada akhir periode Weda, makhluk gaib yang baik disebut Dewa-asura. Dalam sastra Hindu pasca-periode Weda, seperti Purana dan Itihasa, para dewa merupakan makhluk baik, sedangkan asura makhluk jahat. Dalam sejumlah karya sastra India Abad Pertengahan, para dewa juga disebut sebagai "sura", dan sifatnya bertolak belakang dengan saudara tiri mereka yang sama-sama sakti, yang disebut sebagai "asura". Para dewa, demikian pula para asura, yaksa (roh penunggu alam), dan raksasa (monster, setan), merupakan bagian dari mitologi India. Para dewa muncul dalam berbagai kisah-kisah kosmologis dalam agama Hindu. Dalam tradisi Hindu umumnya seperti Adwaita wedanta dan Agama Hindu Dharma, Dewa dipandang sebagai manifestasi Brahman dan enggan dipuja sebagai Tuhan tersendiri dan para dewa setara derajatnya dengan dewa lain. Namun dalam filsafat Hindu Dwaita, para dewa tertentu memiliki sekte tertentu pula yang memujanya sebagai Dewa tertinggi. Dalam hal ini, beberapa sekte memiliki paham monoteisme terhadap Dewa tertentu (lihat: Waisnawa).
description.en: Deva (Sanskrit: देव, Sanskrit pronunciation: [de:ʋɐ]) means 'god', 'shiny', 'exalted', 'heavenly being', 'divine being', 'anything of excellence', and is also one of the Sanskrit terms used to indicate a deity in Hinduism. Deva is a masculine term; the feminine equivalent is Devi. The word is a cognate with Latin deus ('god') and Greek Zeus. In the earliest Vedic literature, all supernatural beings are called Devas and Asuras. The concepts and legends evolved in ancient Indian literature, and by the late Vedic period, benevolent supernatural beings are referred to as Deva-Asuras. In post-Vedic Hindu texts, such as the Puranas and the Itihasas of Hinduism, the Devas represent the good, and the Asuras the bad. In some medieval works of Indian literature, Devas are also referred to as Suras and contrasted with their equally powerful but malevolent half-brothers, referred to as the Asuras. Devas, along with Asuras, Yakshas (nature spirits), and Rakshasas (ghoulish ogres/demons), are part of Indian mythology, and Devas feature in many cosmological theories in Hinduism.

description.en: Djall or Dreq is the personification of evil in Albanian mythology and folklore. The name is used also for a demon of fire. Various tales woven through the years have pitched Djall as the antagonist, the villainous element against which heroes and ordinary people alike must contend. As a symbolic representation of evil forces, Djall serves to highlight the contrasting virtues of courage, wisdom, and moral integrity in those who dare to oppose it. But Djall is no mere metaphor, in these narratives, it takes a form that can manifest in the physical world, most terrifyingly as a fire demon. This elemental characteristic adds another layer of peril to its already fearsome existence. A walking inferno, it brings both moral and mortal danger.

description.en: In Norse mythology, Dökkálfar ("Dark Elves") and Ljósálfar ("Light Elves") are two contrasting types of elves; the dark elves dwell within the earth and have a dark complexion, while the light elves live in Álfheimr, and are "fairer than the sun to look at". The Ljósálfar and the Dökkálfar are attested in the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson, and in the late Old Norse poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins. Scholars have produced theories about the origin and implications of the dualistic concept.

description.id: Dōsojin (道祖神, "dewa pelindung jalan") adalah nama yang umum bagi sejenis kami yang populer dipuja di wilayah Kantō dan area di sekitarnya. Sebagai dewa pelindung perbatasan, umat Shinto percaya bahwa mereka melindungi para pelancong dan penduduk dari wabah penyakit dan gangguan roh jahat. Mereka juga disebut Sae no kami atau Sai no kami (障の神・塞の神), Dōrokujin (道陸神) atau Shakujin (石神, "dewa batu"). Sering kali dilambangkan sebagai manusia berpasangan, tetapi dibuat patungnya dalam wujud alat kelamin pria dan wanita, dalam bentuk batu besar atau patung, atau bahkan pilar tinggi di sepanjang jalan. Kadang kala dōsojin dikuilkan di sebuah kuil kecil di pinggir jalan yang disebut hokora. Dalam bentuk seperti falus, mereka dihubungkan dengan kelahiran dan penciptaan, dan oleh karena itu sebagai harmoni perkawinan.
description.en: Dōsojin (道祖神) are a class of protective Shinto deities (kami) commonly venerated in eastern Japan, particularly in the Kantō, Chūbu, and Tōhoku regions. They are associated with liminal spaces such as village boundaries, crossroads, and mountain passes, and are believed to ward off evil spirits, epidemics, and other harmful influences that threaten individuals or communities during transitional stages of life.2 Dōsojin (道祖神; literally, "road ancestor deity") is a generic name for a type of Shinto kami popularly worshipped in Kantō and neighboring areas in Japan where, as tutelary deities of borders and paths, they are believed to protect travellers, pilgrims, villages, and individuals in "transitional stages" from epidemics and evil spirits. Also called Sae no kami or Sai no kami (障の神・塞の神), Dōrokujin (道陸神) or Shakujin (石神; literally: "stone kami"). Dōsojin are often represented as a human couple, carved male or female genitals, large stones or statues, or even tall poles along a road. Dōsojin are sometimes housed in small roadside Shinto shrines called hokora. In rural areas Dōsojin can be found at village boundaries, in mountain passes, or along byways, and in urban areas they can be seen at street corners or near bridges. When shaped like a phallus, they are associated with birth, procreation, and marital harmony. When represented as a human couple, Dōsojin are revered as deities of boundaries, roads, travellers, villagers, marriage, fertility, health, agriculture, harvest, procreation, guardianship, defense and protection. They were used as protective markers in village boundaries as fertility symbols for the ensure of the growth of crops.

description.id: Long Wang atau Raja Naga adalah dewa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang dipuja sebagai penguasa lautan. Mereka dapat berubah wujud menjadi manusia dan tinggal dalam istana kristal di dasar laut. Mereka memiliki birokrasi istana tersendiri serta memimpin pasukan yang terdiri atas berbagai makluk laut. Selain berhubungan dengan kehidupan laut, Long Wang juga mampu memanipulasi cuaca dan menurunkan hujan. Para Raja Naga sering muncul dalam berbagai literatur Tiongkok klasik dan istana mereka digambarkan sangat megah. Konon, para Long Wang dulunya adalah ikan mas yang cukup kuat untuk melompati Gerbang Naga, yang dibangun Yu yang Agung dalam usahanya mengendalikan banjir besar di Tiongkok kuno. Mereka dipercaya menguasai air yang bergerak, seperti air terjun, sungai, dan lautan. Mereka dapat mewujudkan diri sebagai semburan air (tornado atau pusaran di atas air). Sebagai penguasa air dan cuaca, para naga memiliki wujud yang lebih antromorfis, sering kali ditampilkan dalam wujud menyerupai manusia, mengenakan jubah serta mahkota raja, tetapi tetap berkepala naga.
description.en: The Dragon King, also known as the Dragon God, is a celestial creature, water and weather god in Asian mythology. They can be found in various cultural and religious symbolic materials all around Asia, specifically in South, Southeast Asia and distinctly in East Asian cultures (Chinese folk-religion). He is known in many different names across Asia depending on the local language such as, Ryū in Japanese. (Korean Dragon, Indian Dragon, Vietnamese Dragon and more) He can manipulate and control the weather, move seasons and bring rainfall with his divine power at his own will, thus, he is regarded as the dispenser of rain, divine ruler of the Seas, rivers and water bodies, commanding over all bodies of water. He is the collective personification of the ancient concept of the lóng in Chinese culture and Nāgarāja in Indian culture. It is described that they have their own under-water palace and a royal court system of their own. There are also the cosmological "Dragon Kings of the Four Seas" (四海龍王; Sihai Longwang). Besides being a water deity, the Dragon God frequently also serves as a territorial tutelary deity, similarly to Tudigong "Lord of the Earth" and Houtu "Queen of the Earth". Serpent like creatures have been regarded as core part of Asian culture since 7000–5000 BCE (Neolithic period) at least. Numerous Serpent like crafts, marks and designs have been discovered in many archeological sites from south, southeast and east asia (Notably from ancient archeological sites of China and India), which proves that the serpent/naga/dragon symbolically has been part of the local folklores, rituals and festivals in these areas from a really long time. As time has passed the Dragon culture has been adapted and shifted in various forms, terms, tales and cultures through generation around these regions and the folk-religious cultures.

description.en: The Drak (German: [dʁaːk]), Drâk, Dråk, Drakel or Fürdrak (either "for-Drak" or "fire Drak"), in Oldenburg also Drake (f.), is a household spirit from German folklore often identified with the Kobold or the devil (German Teufel), both of which are also used as synonymous terms for Drak. Otherwise it is also known as Drache (dragon) but has nothing much to do with the reptilian monster in general.

claims.quote: Das Erscheinungsbild eines Drak ist das eines kleinen Drachen mit glühendem Schweif, mit dem er durch die Lüfte zieht. Im östlichen Pommern kennt man ihn als Alf und mancherorts auch als feurige Schlange mit Entenkopf oder als glühenden Kessel mit Schwanz.

claims.statement_id: Drak bisa berubah wujud menjadi batang kayu menyala berkepala lebar, atau hewan seperti angsa kelabu dan ayam basah; dengan seruan tertentu seperti "Halb Part" atau "lat fallen, wat nich dien hört" ia bisa dipaksa menjatuhkan sebagian hartanya.
claims.quote: Er kann aber auch die Gestalt ändern und erscheint dann als feuriger Wiesbaum mit breitem Kopf ... er kann sich aber auch in Tiere verwandeln, zum Beispiel in eine graue Gans oder ein nasses Huhn. Man kann ihn, mithilfe bestimmter Formeln, dazu zwingen einen Teil seiner Schätze abzuwerfen. Beispiele für solche Formeln sind Halb Part oder lat fallen, wat nich dien hört

claims.statement: Drac or Drak is a household spirit of German folklore that brings wealth to the home it lives in.

claims.quote: Drac, Drak či Drachen, je domácí duch z německého folklóru, který přináší do domácnosti, kterou obývá, bohatství.

claims.statement: Drac flies through the air and enters by the chimney or a hole in the roof; it takes the form of a burning pole, a little man in a red vest, or an animal such as a hen or lizard, at times a fireball; it is closely bound to fire and lives in the hearth or deep in the oven.

claims.quote: Drac létá vzduchem a do domu vstupuje skrze komín či díru ve střeše. Má podobu hořícího bidla, mužíčka v červené vestě, nebo zvířete jako kuře, kohout či ještěrka. Jindy vypadá jako ohnivá koule či planoucí hvězda. Je úzce spjat s ohněm, což vedlo k ztotožňování s ďáblem, a přebývá v krbu nebo hluboko v peci.

claims.statement: Drac is gained through a pact with the devil or hatches from a yolkless egg; it must be fed cakes, meat, milk or millet porridge, and if unfed it takes revenge, usually by setting a fire.
claims.statement_id: Drac diperoleh lewat perjanjian dengan iblis atau menetas dari telur tanpa kuning; ia harus diberi makan kue, daging, susu, atau bubur jawawut, dan bila tidak diberi makan ia membalas dendam, biasanya dengan menyulut kebakaran.

Draca bylo nutno živit, podávaly se mu tak pokrmy jako koláče, maso, mléko nebo jáhlová kaše. Když není krmen, tak se mstí, typicky založením požáru.

claims.quote: Es ist wahrscheinlich, dass der Glaube an den Drak durch Beobachtungen von Meteoriten, Sternschnuppen, Nordlicht oder dem Feuerschein eines Kamins entstand.

claims.statement: In his novel Die Heiden von Kummerow, Ehm Welk describes a Drak supposedly kept by the wicked miller Düker.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Die Heiden von Kummerow, Ehm Welk menggambarkan Drak yang konon dipelihara si penggiling jahat Düker.
claims.quote: Ehm Welk beschreibt in seinem Roman Die Heiden von Kummerow das Wesen eines Draks, welchen angeblich der böse Müller Düker beherbergt.

claims.statement: Grain was protected from the Drac's theft by laying sheaves crosswise in each corner of the barn.
claims.statement_id: Gandum dilindungi dari pencurian Drac dengan menyusun berkas gandum bersilang di setiap sudut lumbung.
claims.quote: Obilí se před krádeží dracem mělo chránit vyskládáním snopů v každém z rohů stodoly do kříže.

description.en: In German folklore, a drude (German: Drude, German: [ˈdʁuːdə], pl. Druden) is a kind of malevolent female nocturnal spirit in Germanic mythology, a sort of alp or witch-hag associated with nightmares, prevalent especially in Southern Germany. It also occurs in the form or trude.

claims.statement: In German folklore the drude is a malevolent female nocturnal spirit of Germanic mythology, a sort of Alp or witch-hag tied to nightmares, prevalent in southern Germany, also called trude.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, drude adalah sejenis roh malam perempuan yang jahat dalam mitologi Jermanik, semacam Alp atau nenek sihir yang dikaitkan dengan mimpi buruk, terutama di Jerman selatan, dan juga disebut trude.
claims.quote: is a kind of malevolent female nocturnal spirit in Germanic mythology, a sort of alp or witch-hag associated with nightmares, prevalent especially in Southern Germany. It also occurs in the form or trude .

claims.statement: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German, and in the 16th century trute also became a general term for 'witch'.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini tercatat sebagai trute dalam bahasa Jerman Hulu Pertengahan akhir, dan pada abad ke-16 trute juga dipakai sebagai sebutan umum untuk "penyihir".
claims.quote: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German. ... The word trute also came to be used as a generic term for "witch" in the 16th century (Hans Sachs).

claims.statement: Middle High German trute relates to Old Norse troða ('to tread, trample') and German treten, the etymology deemed most plausible; in later Bavarian tradition the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder, Trudner or Truderer.
claims.statement_id: Kata Jerman Hulu Pertengahan trute berkaitan dengan Nordik Kuno troða ("menginjak, menginjak-injak") dan kata Jerman modern treten, etimologi yang dianggap paling masuk akal; dalam tradisi Bayern kemudian, Trude perempuan punya pasangan lelaki bernama Truder, Trudner, atau Truderer.
claims.quote: Middle High German trute is etymologically related to Old Norse troða ("to tread, to trample"), i.e., is related to modern German verb treten ("to tread, to step"); this is considered the most plausible etymology in modern philological opinion. ... In later Bavarian folklore tradition, the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder , Trudner , or Truderer

claims.statement: The drude is blamed for the Alpdruck nightmare ('elf pressure') and so counted a subtype of the Alp in attack; in some lore she is a witch who can be small or large, and only her spirit leaves the body to torment sleepers.
claims.statement_id: Drude dianggap penyebab mimpi buruk Alpdruck ("tekanan elf") sehingga dalam cara menyerang dipandang subtipe Alp; menurut sebagian cerita ia penyihir yang bisa berukuran kecil atau besar, dan konon hanya rohnya yang keluar dari tubuh untuk menyiksa orang yang tidur.
claims.quote: Drude is held responsible for causing the nightmare Alpdruck ("elf pressure"), thus considered just a subtype of an Alp, as far as its attack behavior is concerned. According to some folklore, the drude is a witch who can assume various sizes, small or large ... It is also said that only the witch's spirit drifts out of body to perform their handiwork tormenting people (in their sleep).

claims.statement: The Drude (also Drute, Trude, Trute; male Druder or Bavarian Truderer) is a folk-belief being that sits on sleepers' chests at night causing nightmares, oppression and breathlessness; in the Oldenburg area it is called Walrider or Walriderske.
claims.statement_id: Drude (juga Drute, Trude, Trute; lelaki Druder atau dalam bahasa Bayern Truderer) adalah makhluk kepercayaan rakyat yang pada malam hari duduk di dada orang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk, rasa tertekan, dan sesak napas; di Oldenburg ia disebut Walrider atau Walriderske.
claims.quote: Eine Drude (auch Drute, Trude, Trute, Trut, männlich Drud, Druder, Drudner, Trutner oder bairisch Truderer) ist ein Wesen des Volksglaubens, das sich nachts auf die Brust von Schlafenden setzt und Albträume, Beklemmungen und Atemnot verursacht. ... sowie im oldenburgischen Raum Walrider, Walriderske.

claims.statement: As drudes these pressing spirits are widespread in southern Germany and Austria: women condemned to find a victim each night, adults, children, animals, even trees and stones; their soul leaves the body, slips through cracks and keyholes and appears as a cat, straw or feather.
claims.statement_id: Di Jerman selatan dan Austria, drude adalah perempuan yang dikutuk mencari korban setiap malam, orang dewasa, anak, hewan, juga pohon dan batu; rohnya masuk lewat celah dan lubang kunci dan tampil dalam berbagai rupa seperti kucing, sedotan, atau bulu.
claims.quote: Hier sind Frauen, die dazu verdammt sind, sich jede Nacht ein Opfer zum Drücken suchen zu müssen: Erwachsene, Kinder und Haustiere werden heimgesucht, aber auch Bäume und Steine. ... kann als Geist durch kleinste Spalten und Schlüssellöcher in ein Zimmer dringen und dann in verschiedener Gestalt erscheinen (z. B. als Katze, Strohhalm oder Feder).

claims.statement: The magic sign Drudenfuß, also Drudenkreuz, is said to protect against them; by legend it comes from a drude's bird-like footprint.
claims.statement_id: Tanda gaib Drudenfuß, juga disebut Drudenkreuz, konon melindungi dari drude; menurut sage, tanda ini berasal dari jejak kaki drude yang mirip kaki burung.
claims.quote: Das Zauberzeichen Drudenfuß, auch Drudenkreuz genannt, soll gegen sie schützen. Der Ursprung dieses Zeichens liegt der Sage nach im vogelartigen Fußabdruck einer Drude.

claims.statement: Drudensteine (also Hühnergott), pebbles with a natural hole called the 'eye', were also believed to ward drudes off and were hung by a cord in the roof.
claims.statement_id: Drudenstein (juga Hühnergott), kerikil dengan lubang alami yang disebut "mata", juga dipercaya menangkal drude dan digantung dengan tali di rangka atap rumah.
claims.quote: Ebenfalls abwehrende Wirkung sollten Drudensteine (auch Hühnergott genannt) haben, die Kieselsteine mit einem natürlichen Loch, dem sogenannten Auge sind. Diese wurden zur Abwehr mit einem Band oder einer Schnur im Dachstuhl des Hauses aufgehängt.

description.en: The Dungarvon Whooper (pronounced "hooper") is a ghost story told in a song composed by Michael Whelan, about the alleged murder along the Dungarvon River in central New Brunswick, Canada, in the mid to late 19th century.

claims.statement: The Dungarvon Whooper is a ghost story in a song by Michael Whelan about an alleged murder in New Brunswick, Canada.
claims.statement_id: Dungarvon Whooper adalah kisah hantu dalam lagu gubahan Michael Whelan tentang pembunuhan di sungai Dungarvon River, New Brunswick, Canada.
claims.quote: The Dungarvon Whooper (pronounced "hooper") is a ghost story told in a song composed by Michael Whelan, about the alleged murder along the Dungarvon River in central New Brunswick, Canada

claims.statement: The story revolves around a young cook working in a New Brunswick lumber camp along the river.
claims.statement_id: Cerita ini berpusat pada seorang juru masak muda di kamp penebang kayu New Brunswick di sepanjang Dungarvon river.
claims.quote: The story revolves around a young cook working in a New Brunswick lumber camp, along Dungarvon river.

claims.statement: It is described as an invisible ghost, or sometimes as a wildcat or puma-like creature.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya berwujud hantu tak terlihat, tetapi kadang dikatakan menyerupai kucing liar atau puma.
claims.quote: The Dungarvon Whooper's physical description is usually that of an invisible ghost, but it is also sometimes said to resemble a wildcat or puma-like creature

description.en: Dúrnir (Old Norse: [ˈduːrnez̠]) was a dwarf who appears in the three Old Norse skaldic poems which suggests that he once was a well-known dwarf in Norse mythology. The most notable poem is known as Ynglingatal: He also appears in a list of Dwarves in the anonymous Dverga heiti: Alþjófr, austri, aurvangr ok dúfr, ái, andvari, ónn ok draupnir, dori ok dagfinnr, dulinn ok ónarr, alfr ok dellingr, óinn ok durnir. The third poem is found in Laufás-Edda: Kveða skal hróðr fyr hríðar hræ-blakks viðum sævar, drykkr var Durnis rekkum døkkr, ljósara nøkkvi. Snorri also includes Dúrnir in a list of giants in the Skáldskaparmál section of his Prose Edda (Faulkes translation, p. 157). It is possible that the name Durnir is an emendation of Durinn, mentioned as the father of dwarves in Dvergatal. Both names mean door, or door-warden. The names Durinn and Durnir do not appear in the same texts. The Norwegian translation of Ynglinga Saga from 1900 uses the name of Durinn instead of Durnir.

claims.statement: Dúrnir was a dwarf appearing in three Old Norse skaldic poems, suggesting he was once a well-known dwarf in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Dúrnir adalah kurcaci yang muncul dalam tiga puisi skald Nordik Kuno (Old Norse), yang menunjukkan ia dahulu kurcaci terkenal dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse).
claims.quote: was a dwarf who appears in the three Old Norse skaldic poems which suggests that he once was a well-known dwarf in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: Ynglingatal: by Diurnir's (Dúrnir) elfin race, who haunt the cliffs and shun day's face, the valiant Swegde (Sveigðir) was deceived, and the king believed the elf's false words.
claims.statement_id: Ynglingatal: oleh kaum elf keturunan Diurnir (Dúrnir), yang menghuni tebing dan menghindari wajah siang, Swegde (Sveigðir) yang gagah diperdaya, dan sang raja mempercayai kata-kata palsu elf itu.
claims.quote: By Diurnir's elfin race, Who haunt the cliffs and shun day's face, The valiant Swegde was deceived, The elf's false words the king believed.

claims.statement: The dauntless hero rushed through the yawning mouth of stone; it yawned, it shut, and the hero fell in Saekmime's (Sökkmímir) hall, where giants dwell.
claims.statement_id: Pahlawan yang tak gentar itu berlari menembus mulut batu yang menganga; batu itu terbuka lalu menutup, dan sang pahlawan tewas di aula Saekmime (Sökkmímir), tempat para raksasa tinggal.
claims.quote: The dauntless hero rushing on, Passed through the yawning mouth of stone: It yawned – it shut – the hero fell, In Saekmime's hall, where giants dwell.

claims.statement: Snorri also lists Dúrnir among giants in the Skáldskaparmál section of his Prose Edda.
claims.statement_id: Snorri juga memasukkan Dúrnir dalam daftar raksasa di bagian Skáldskaparmál dari Edda Prosa (Prose Edda).
claims.quote: Snorri also includes Dúrnir in a list of giants in the Skáldskaparmál section of his Prose Edda (Faulkes translation, p. 157).

claims.statement: The name Durnir may be an emendation of Durinn, father of the dwarfs in Dvergatal; both mean 'door' or 'door-warden' and do not appear in the same texts.
claims.statement_id: Nama Durnir mungkin emendasi dari Durinn, ayah para kurcaci dalam Dvergatal; kedua nama berarti "pintu" atau "penjaga pintu" dan tidak muncul dalam teks yang sama.
claims.quote: It is possible that the name Durnir is an emendation of Durinn, mentioned as the father of dwarves in Dvergatal. Both names mean door, or door-warden. The names Durinn and Durnir do not appear in the same texts.

claims.statement: He also appears in a list of dwarves in the anonymous Dverga heiti, and the third poem is found in the Laufás-Edda.
claims.statement_id: Dúrnir juga muncul dalam daftar kurcaci dalam Dverga heiti yang anonim, dan puisi ketiga terdapat dalam Laufás-Edda.
claims.quote: He also appears in a list of Dwarves in the anonymous Dverga heiti

description.en: Dzoavits was a demon or ogre from Shoshonean mythology who stole the sun and kidnapped children. He is associated with volcanism and cannibalism. In most legends he confronts several mythological animals before being trapped in a cave, the most common one being Devils Hole.

claims.statement: Dzoavits was a demon or ogre of Shoshonean mythology who stole the sun and kidnapped children.
claims.statement_id: Dzoavits adalah iblis atau raksasa pemakan manusia dalam mitologi Shoshone yang mencuri matahari dan menculik anak-anak.
claims.quote: Dzoavits was a demon or ogre from Shoshonean mythology who stole the sun and kidnapped children.

claims.statement: He is associated with volcanism and cannibalism.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan gunung berapi dan kanibalisme.
claims.quote: He is associated with volcanism and cannibalism.

claims.statement: In most legends he faces several mythological animals before being trapped in a cave, most commonly Devils Hole.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan legenda, ia berhadapan dengan beberapa hewan mitologi sebelum terperangkap di sebuah gua, yang paling sering disebut Devils Hole.
claims.quote: In most legends he confronts several mythological animals before being trapped in a cave, the most common one being Devils Hole.

description.en: Ebajalg (whirlwind) is a being found in Estonian mythology. It is a whirlwind, believed to be a malicious spirit or demon. They are described as having great strength, often leading to destruction.

claims.statement: Ebajalg (whirlwind) is a being of Estonian mythology, a whirlwind believed to be a malicious spirit or demon, described as very strong and often destructive.
claims.statement_id: Ebajalg (angin puting) adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Estonia, berupa pusaran angin yang dipercaya sebagai roh atau iblis jahat; digambarkan sangat kuat dan sering merusak.
claims.quote: Ebajalg (whirlwind) is a being found in Estonian mythology. It is a whirlwind, believed to be a malicious spirit or demon. They are described as having great strength, often leading to destruction.

claims.statement: Tuulispask (also vihur or ebajalg) is the folk name for a strong whirlwind moving over land.
claims.statement_id: Tuulispask (juga vihur atau ebajalg) adalah nama rakyat untuk pusaran angin kuat yang bergerak di atas daratan.
claims.quote: Tuulispask (ka vihur või ebajalg) on rahvapärane nimetus maismaa kohal liikuva tugeva tuulekeerise kohta.

claims.statement: In Estonian folk belief the whirlwind was commonly imagined to be caused by the soul of a person (a witch) temporarily out of the body, more rarely the soul of a dead person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Estonia lazim dibayangkan bahwa pusaran angin ditimbulkan jiwa manusia (penyihir) yang sementara meninggalkan tubuhnya, lebih jarang jiwa orang mati.
claims.quote: Eesti rahvausundis oli levinud kujutelm, et keeristuult tekitab inimese(nõia) kehast ajutiselt lahkunud hing, harvem surnud inimese hing.

claims.statement: The whirlwind could also be a being made or sent by a witch; among the Seto it was the devil, his son or mother; it carried off grain and hay from others' fields, also luck, brought illness and did other harm.
claims.statement_id: Pusaran angin juga bisa makhluk yang dibuat atau dikirim penyihir; di kalangan Seto ia iblis, anaknya, atau ibunya; ia membawa pergi gandum dan jerami dari ladang orang lain, juga keberuntungan, membawa penyakit, dan berbuat jahat lainnya.
claims.quote: Tuulispask võis olla ka nõia tehtud või saadetud olevus, setudel kurat, selle poeg või ema. Uskumuse järgi viis ta võõrastelt põldudelt ära vilja, heina jms, kuid võis ära viia ka õnne, tuua haigust ja teha muud halba.

claims.statement: According to Matthias Johann Eisen, in the south the tuulispask is also called ebajalg; the ebajalg shows great strength, even carrying off haystacks.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Matthias Johann Eisen, di selatan tuulispask disebut juga ebajalg; ebajalg menunjukkan kekuatan sangat besar, bahkan membawa pergi tumpukan jerami.
claims.quote: Lõuna pool nimetatakse tuulispaska ka ebajalaks. Ebajalg avaldab iseäranis suurt jõudu, viib isegi heinasaod ja -kuhjad kaasa.

claims.statement: The whirlwind was warded off magically; a common method was to throw a bladed tool into it, hoping that hitting the soul would also wound the person's body.
claims.statement_id: Pusaran angin ditangkal dengan cara magis; cara yang sering dipakai adalah melempar benda tajam ke pusaran, berharap jiwa yang terkena membuat tubuh orang itu ikut terluka.
claims.quote: Tuulispaska tõrjuti maagiliste võtetega. Sageli kasutatud võte oli visata keerist mõne terariistaga, lootes, et nii hinge tabades saab vigastatud ka vastava isiku keha.

description.en: In the Old Norse religion, Eitri (Old Norse: [ˈɛitre]; or Sindri) is a dwarf and the brother of Brokkr. According to Skáldskaparmál, when Loki had Sif's hair, Freyr's ship Skidbladnir and Odin's spear Gungnir fashioned by the Sons of Ivaldi, he bet his own head with Brokkr that Eitri would not have been able to make items that matched the craftsmanship of those mentioned above. Eitri began working in his furnace while his brother was working the bellows, but a fly (sometimes thought to be Loki himself) began stinging Brokkr, trying to stop him and spoil the items. Eitri succeeded in making the golden boar Gullinbursti, the golden ring Draupnir, and the hammer Mjöllnir that made his brother win the bet, even if its handle was shorter than it should have been.

claims.statement: Eitri, also called Sindri, is a dwarf and Brokkr's brother in Old Norse religion.

claims.quote: or Sindri) is a dwarf and the brother of Brokkr.

claims.statement_id: Eitri (atau Sindri) adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik, saudara Brokk.
claims.quote: Eitri (ou Sindri) est un nain de la mythologie nordique. Il a pour frère Brokk.

claims.statement: In the Marvel Cinematic Universe Eitri is a supporting character played by Peter Dinklage, mainly in Avengers: Infinity War, living on Nidavellir.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Marvel Cinematic Universe, Eitri adalah tokoh pendukung yang diperankan aktor Peter Dinklage, terutama dalam film Avengers: Infinity War, dan tinggal di Nidavellir.

description.en: En-Naddāha (Egyptian Arabic: النداهة "the caller") is an Egyptian legend of a naiad-like female spirit who calls men to the Nile, leading to their death or disappearance. It is especially well known in the rural and agriculture-based areas of Egypt along the Nile and the Nile's water canals.

claims.statement: El Naddaha is a female spirit in Egyptian legend who calls men to the Nile, leading to death or disappearance.
claims.statement_id: El Naddaha adalah roh perempuan dalam legenda Mesir yang memanggil laki-laki ke Nil hingga mati atau menghilang.
claims.quote: En-Naddāha (Egyptian Arabic: النداهة "the caller") is an Egyptian legend of a naiad-like female spirit who calls men to the Nile, leading to their death or disappearance. It is especially well known in the rural and agriculture-based areas of Egypt along the Nile and the Nile's water canals.

claims.statement: The legend’s origin is uncertain and it is more popular in rural settings.
claims.statement_id: Asal legenda ini tidak pasti dan lebih populer dalam lingkungan pedesaan.
claims.quote: The exact origin of this legend is unknown. The story was more popular during the 20th century when Egypt was less urban than it is now, and people would spend more time close to the Nile and the Nile's water canals. Children would play by its shores after school, and young men would chat there at night.

claims.statement: She calls men by name and makes them follow her voice in a hypnotized state.
claims.statement_id: Ia memanggil laki-laki dengan nama mereka dan membuat mereka mengikuti suaranya dalam keadaan terhipnosis.
claims.quote: En-Naddaha takes the form of stunningly beautiful woman who appears, as if by chance, to men walking by the Nile or the Nile's water canals at night. The men are usually a pair. The creature calls one by his first name, rendering him speechless, hypnotized, and obedient to her voice which he blindly follows, while the other man is unaffected, and attempts to pull the other back.

claims.statement: She is depicted as a beautiful young woman with long hair and loose clothing.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda cantik dengan rambut panjang dan busana longgar.
claims.quote: Usually the men do not get close enough to the Nile to get a glimpse of what the creature looks like before they run away. In rare instances, they get a glimpse of her. She is described as being a very beautiful young woman; tall, slender, with long flowing hair down her back.

claims.statement: Some tales delay the victim’s departure for several nights after the call.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menunda keberangkatan korban sampai beberapa malam setelah panggilan.
claims.quote: In rural Egypt, where the legend is prominent, the creature may call for men in their homes by the shores of the Nile and the Nile's water canals, who then eagerly attempt to leave home for her. In other tales, the affected man will not immediately try to follow, but he will enter a state of disturbed distraction for a few nights before at last departing late at night.

description.en: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being that is described in occult and alchemical works from around the time of the European Renaissance, and particularly elaborated in the 16th century works of Paracelsus. According to Paracelsus and his subsequent followers, there are four categories of elementals, which are gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders. These correspond to the four Empedoclean elements of antiquity: earth, water, air, and fire, respectively. Terms employed for beings associated with alchemical elements vary by source and gloss.

claims.statement: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being described in occult and alchemical works from around the European Renaissance, especially developed in Paracelsus's 16th-century writings.
claims.statement_id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib mitis yang digambarkan dalam karya okultisme dan alkimia sekitar masa Renaisans Eropa, terutama dikembangkan dalam karya Paracelsus abad ke-16.
claims.quote: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being that is described in occult and alchemical works from around the time of the European Renaissance, and particularly elaborated in the 16th century works of Paracelsus.

claims.statement: According to Paracelsus and his followers there are four kinds of elementals, gnomes, undines, sylphs and salamanders, matching the four Empedoclean elements: earth, water, air and fire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Paracelsus dan pengikutnya, ada empat jenis elemental, yaitu gnome, undine, sylph, dan salamander, yang sesuai dengan empat unsur Empedokles: tanah, air, udara, dan api.
claims.quote: According to Paracelsus and his subsequent followers, there are four categories of elementals, which are gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders. These correspond to the four Empedoclean elements of antiquity: earth, water, air, and fire, respectively.

claims.statement: In his Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus assigned mythological beings to the four elements; part of the Philosophia Magna, it was first printed in 1566 after his death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus menggolongkan makhluk mitologis ke dalam empat unsur; buku ini bagian Philosophia Magna dan pertama dicetak pada 1566 setelah ia wafat.
claims.quote: In his 16th-century work A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus identified mythological beings as belonging to one of the four elements. Part of the Philosophia Magna, this book was first printed in 1566 after Paracelsus' death.

claims.statement: The concept of elementals seems to have been devised by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not actually use the word 'elemental' or a German equivalent.
claims.statement_id: Konsep elemental tampaknya diciptakan Paracelsus pada abad ke-16, walau ia sendiri tidak memakai istilah elemental atau padanannya dalam bahasa Jerman.
claims.quote: The concept of elementals seems to have been conceived by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not in fact use the term "elemental" or a German equivalent.

claims.statement: He saw them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, usually invisible to humans yet with physical, mostly humanlike bodies, eating, sleeping and wearing clothes like people.
claims.statement_id: Ia menganggap mereka bukan roh semata, melainkan makhluk di antara makhluk jasmani dan roh, biasanya tak terlihat manusia tetapi bertubuh jasmani mirip manusia, makan, tidur, dan berpakaian seperti manusia.
claims.quote: He regarded them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, generally being invisible to mankind but having physical and commonly humanoid bodies, as well as eating, sleeping, and wearing clothes like humans.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the idea of elemental spirits comes from late-antique Neoplatonism and was revived by early modern natural philosophers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, gagasan roh unsur berasal dari Neoplatonisme akhir zaman kuno dan dihidupkan kembali para filsuf alam awal zaman modern.
claims.quote: Die Vorstellung von Elementargeistern stammt ursprünglich aus dem spätantiken Neuplatonismus und wurde von frühneuzeitlichen Naturphilosophen wieder aufgegriffen.

claims.statement: Elemental spirits are figures of natural philosophy and literature and do not occur in folk belief or folk tales.
claims.statement_id: Roh unsur adalah tokoh filsafat alam dan sastra, bukan bagian kepercayaan atau cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Elementargeister sind Gestalten der Naturphilosophie und der Literatur, in Volksglauben und Volkserzählungen kommen sie nicht vor.

claims.statement: They also play a role in various forms of neopaganism and modern esotericism, such as anthroposophy.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga berperan dalam berbagai bentuk neopaganisme dan esoterisme modern, misalnya antroposofi.
claims.quote: Elementargeister spielen auch in verschiedenen Formen von Neuheidentum und moderner Esoterik eine Rolle, etwa in der Anthroposophie.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, Montfaucon de Villars's occult novel Le Comte de Gabalis (Paris, 1670) has its title character discuss marriage with the 'peoples of the four elements'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, novel okultisme Montfaucon de Villars, Le Comte de Gabalis (Paris, 1670), memuat tokoh Comte de Gabalis yang membahas pernikahan dengan "bangsa empat unsur".
claims.quote: その1世紀後にパリで出版されたモンフォーコン・ド・ヴィラール ... の隠秘学小説『ガバリス伯爵』（1670年）は、作中人物のガバリス伯爵をして「四大の民」との婚姻について語らしめた。

description.en: The Elbedritsch - also Elwetrittche, Ilwedritsch; in the plural Elwedritsche(n) - is an imaginary bird-like creature that is reported in southwest Germany (especially in the Palatinate and neighboring regions). The area of distribution is essentially congruent with the historical Palatinate. With emigrants, the belief in the existence of Elbedritsche also spread to Eastern Europe and North America (Pennsylvania) in the 18th century and to South America (Brazil) in the 19th century. The Elbedritsch is to be seen as a local variation on comparable imaginary creatures from other regions (cf. Wolpertinger). The oldest written mention to date comes from Luckenbach, Texas. In 1847, sources reported that an “Elfendritschenwolpertinger” had been seen by German hunters in the woods around South Grape Creek.

claims.statement: The Elwetritsch is an imaginary bird-like creature reported in south-western Germany (especially the Palatinate and nearby); with emigrants the belief spread to Eastern Europe and North America (Pennsylvania) in the 18th century and to South America (Brazil) in the 19th.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch (juga Elwetrittche, Ilwedritsch) adalah makhluk khayalan mirip burung yang dikabarkan di barat daya Jerman (terutama Pfalz dan sekitarnya); bersama emigran, kepercayaan ini menyebar ke Eropa Timur dan Amerika Utara (Pennsylvania) pada abad ke-18 dan ke Amerika Selatan (Brasil) pada abad ke-19.
claims.quote: also Elwetrittche, Ilwedritsch; in the plural Elwedritsche(n) - is an imaginary bird-like creature that is reported in southwest Germany (especially in the Palatinate and neighboring regions). ... With emigrants, the belief in the existence of Elbedritsche also spread to Eastern Europe and North America (Pennsylvania) in the 18th century and to South America (Brazil) in the 19th century.

claims.statement: The Elwetritsch (mock-scientific Latin Bestia palatinensis) is a bird-like fabulous creature of south-western Germany, especially the Palatinate, seen as the local counterpart of the Bavarian Wolpertinger or Thuringian Rasselbock.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch (dalam Latin semu ilmiah Bestia palatinensis) adalah makhluk khayalan mirip burung dari barat daya Jerman, terutama Pfalz, dan dianggap padanan lokal Wolpertinger dari Bayern atau Rasselbock dari Thüringen.
claims.quote: in pseudowissenschaftlichem Latein Bestia palatinensis) ist ein vogelähnliches Fabelwesen, von dem in Südwestdeutschland und vor allem in der Pfalz berichtet wird. Die Elwetritsch ist als lokale Entsprechung zu Fabelwesen anderer Regionen anzusehen, wie dem bayerischen Wolpertinger oder dem thüringischen Rasselbock.

claims.statement: Elwetritschen are described as broadly chicken-like but said to be barely able to use their wings, so they keep to underbrush or under vines; they are sometimes shown with deer antlers and a very long beak.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch digambarkan mirip ayam, tetapi konon hampir tak bisa memakai sayapnya sehingga harus tinggal di semak belukar atau di bawah tanaman anggur; kadang digambarkan bertanduk rusa dan berparuh sangat panjang.
claims.quote: Elwetritschen werden als im weitesten Sinne hühnerähnlich beschrieben. Allerdings heißt es, sie könnten ihre Flügel kaum gebrauchen, weshalb sie sich überwiegend im Unterholz oder unter den Rebstöcken aufhalten müssten. Manchmal werden Elwetritschen auch mit einem Hirschgeweih abgebildet, ihr Schnabel wird oft als sehr lang dargestellt.

claims.statement: Elwetritschen are said to come from crossing chickens, ducks and geese with forest kobolds and elves; as poultry offspring they lay eggs, which because of their forest-spirit descent grow during brooding.
claims.statement_id: Elwetritsch konon berasal dari persilangan ayam, bebek, dan angsa dengan kobold dan peri penghuni hutan; sebagai keturunan unggas ia bertelur, tetapi karena darah roh hutannya, telurnya tumbuh selama masa pengeraman.
claims.quote: Elwetritschen sollen aus Kreuzungen von Hühnern, Enten und Gänsen mit im Wald lebenden Kobolden und Elfen stammen. Als Geflügelabkömmlinge legen sie selbstverständlich Eier, die allerdings wegen der Waldgeisterherkunft während der Brutzeit wachsen.

claims.statement: In many Palatinate villages tourists are offered an Elwetritsch hunting licence for fun; the best time is dark new-moon nights, and in one variant the catcher needs a sack, an oil lamp and a club.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak desa Pfalz, wisatawan ditawari izin berburu Elwetritsch sebagai hiburan; waktu berburu terbaik malam gelap saat bulan baru, dan dalam satu cara penangkap memerlukan karung, lampu minyak, dan pentung.
claims.quote: In etlichen pfälzischen Gemeinden wird Touristen als launiger Zeitvertreib der Erwerb eines Elwetritschen-Jagdscheins angeboten. ... Die günstigste Jagdzeit sind dunkle Neumond­nächte. Bei einer Variante der Jagd benötigt der Fänger einen Sack, eine Öllampe und einen Knüppel.

claims.statement: Beaters shout 'tritsch, tritsch' and strike trees or vineyard posts to flush the creatures into the sack; the often unsuspecting catcher is sometimes secretly left outdoors until he gets home frozen and empty-handed.
claims.statement_id: Para penghalau berteriak "tritsch, tritsch" dan memukul pohon atau tiang kebun anggur agar Elwetritsch lari ke karung; penangkap yang sering tak curiga kadang ditinggalkan diam-diam di luar sampai pulang kedinginan tanpa hasil.
claims.quote: Treiber versuchen, durch lautes „Tritsch, tritsch“-Rufen und durch Stockschläge gegen Bäume oder Weinbergspfähle die Elwetritschen aufzuscheuchen, damit sie in den Sack des Fängers flüchten. ... Der häufig ahnungslose Fänger und Jagdscheinaspirant wird gelegentlich heimlich im Freien zurückgelassen, bis er endlich durchgefroren – und ohne Jagdbeute – heimfindet.

claims.statement: One reading holds the second part of the name unclear, while the first refers to elves or Elben, female forest spirits of Germanic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Satu tafsiran menganggap asal bagian kedua nama itu tidak jelas, sedangkan bagian pertama merujuk pada elf atau Elben, roh hutan perempuan dalam mitologi Jermanik.
claims.quote: Eine Deutung geht davon aus, die Herkunft des zweiten Wortteils sei unklar und strittig, während der erste Bezug nehme auf die Elfen beziehungsweise Elben als weibliche Waldgeister aus der germanischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: The oldest written mention comes from Luckenbach, Texas: in 1847 sources reported German hunters had seen an 'Elfendritschenwolpertinger' in the woods around South Grape Creek.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis tertua berasal dari Luckenbach, Texas: pada 1847 sumber melaporkan para pemburu Jerman melihat seekor "Elfendritschenwolpertinger" di hutan sekitar South Grape Creek.
claims.quote: The oldest written mention to date comes from Luckenbach, Texas. In 1847, sources reported that an “Elfendritschenwolpertinger” had been seen by German hunters in the woods around South Grape Creek.

claims.statement: To protect themselves from Elwetritsch attacks, hunters drink plenty of alcohol before and during the hunt, its smell supposedly keeping the creatures away.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi diri dari serangan Elwetritsch, para pemburu minum banyak alkohol sebelum dan selama perburuan, yang baunya konon menjauhkan makhluk itu.
claims.quote: Um sich vor Angriffen der Elwetritschen zu schützen, trinken die Jäger vor und während der Jagd reichlich Alkohol, dessen Geruch angeblich die Elwetritschen auf Distanz hält.

description.en: The Enfield Monster is an unidentified creature reported around Enfield, Illinois, United States in April 1973. The reports were covered by the news media at the time, with some suggesting they may have been caused by a wild ape or escaped kangaroo. Used as a case study for a paper on social contagion in 1978, the episode is cited by sociologists as an example of collective behavior where a group or crowd can be affected by the spread of "group emotions" such as "panics, hysterias, collective visions, and extreme instances of suggestibility."

description.en: In European folklore and myth, the Erlking is a sinister elf who lingers in the woods. He stalks children who stay in the woods for too long and kills them with a single touch. The name "Erlking" (German: Erlkönig, lit. 'alder-king'; German: [ˈɛʁlkøːnɪç, -nɪk]) is a name used in German Romanticism for the figure of a spirit or "king of the fairies". It is usually assumed that the name is a derivation from the ellekonge (older elverkonge, i.e. "Elf-king") in Danish folklore. The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in his ballad Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), an adaptation of the Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), and was taken up by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in his poem Erlkönig (1782), which was set to music by Schubert and others. Goethe added a new meaning, as "Erl" means not "elf" but "black alder", and the poem about the Erlenkönig is set in the area of an alder quarry in the Saale Valley, in Thuringia. In English translations of Goethe's poem, the name is sometimes rendered as Erl-king.

claims.statement: In Herder's telling Sir Oluf rides to his wedding but is drawn by elfin music; the Ellerkonge's daughter invites him to dance, he refuses her and her gifts of gold, the furious elf strikes him down, and next morning his bride finds him dead.

claims.quote: un homme du nom de Sir Oluf chevauchant pour son mariage mais attiré par la musique des elfes. Une elfe vierge, la fille du Ellerkonge, apparaît et l'invite à danser avec elle. Il refuse la proposition et son offre de cadeaux et d'or. Furieuse, elle le frappe et le fait tomber à terre. Le lendemain matin, le jour de son mariage, son épouse le trouve à cet endroit, mort

description.id: Peri merupakan istilah yang sering digunakan dalam cerita rakyat, dongeng, dan fiksi Eropa untuk menggambarkan makhluk yang mempunyai kekuatan gaib yang kadang kala turut campur dalam urusan-urusan manusia. Istilah peri dalam bahasa Indonesia sering digunakan dalam penerjemahan tokoh yang menggambarkannya sebagai elf atau fairy (istilah dalam bahasa Inggris) dalam cerita fiksi maupun dongeng-dongeng dari Eropa. Pada kisah fiksi modern karakter Peri sering dipinjam dari versi aslinya dan digunakan dalam kisah fiksi fantasi masa kini dengan berbagai variasi penggambaran tergantung oleh penulis atau penciptanya.
description.en: A fairy (also fay or faerie/faery) is a type of mythical being or legendary creature, generally described as anthropomorphic, found in the folklore of multiple European cultures (including Celtic, Slavic, Germanic, and French folklore), a form of spirit, often with magical, metaphysical, supernatural, or preternatural qualities. Myths and stories about fairies do not have a single origin but are rather a collection of folk beliefs from disparate sources. Various folk theories about the origins of fairies include casting them as either demoted angels or demons in a Christian tradition, as deities in pagan belief systems, as spirits of the dead, as prehistoric precursors to humans, or as spirits of nature. The label of fairy has at times applied only to specific magical creatures with human appearance, magical powers, and a penchant for trickery. At other times, it has been used to describe any magical creature, such as goblins and gnomes. Fairy has at times been used as an adjective, with a meaning equivalent to "enchanted" or "magical". It was also used as a name for the place these beings come from: Fairyland. A recurring motif of legends about fairies is the need to ward off fairies using protective charms. Common examples of such charms include church bells, wearing clothing inside out, four-leaf clover, and food. Fairies were also sometimes thought to haunt specific locations and to lead travelers astray using will-o'-the-wisps. Before the advent of modern medicine, fairies were often blamed for sickness, particularly tuberculosis and birth deformities. In addition to their folkloric origins, fairies were a common feature of Renaissance literature and Romantic art and were especially popular in the United Kingdom during the Victorian and Edwardian eras. The Celtic Revival also saw fairies established as a canonical part of Celtic cultural heritage.

claims.statement: Fairy refers to supernatural beings said to interfere magically in human affairs.
claims.statement_id: Fairy adalah istilah bagi makhluk gaib yang dalam cerita turut campur secara ajaib dalam urusan manusia.
claims.quote: the common term for a supposed race of supernatural beings who magically intermeddle in human affairs.

claims.statement: Fairies appear in old British and Irish folk narratives.
claims.statement_id: Fairy tampil dalam cerita rakyat lama Britania dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: Discover the intriguing, formidable faeries of old British and Irish folk narratives.

claims.statement: Fairy size and type vary among local stories.
claims.statement_id: Ukuran dan jenis fairy berbeda menurut kisah setempat.
claims.quote: Split between numerous local species, ranging from full-sized Scottish elf-queens to small, wizened male house fairies, they share a number of common characteristics.

claims.statement: In British and Irish tales, fairies are immortal and can vanish, shapeshift, or create illusions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita Britania dan Irlandia, fairy bersifat abadi dan dapat menghilang, berubah wujud, atau menciptakan ilusi.
claims.quote: All are immortal, with supernatural powers that include vanishing, shape-shifting and creating illusions.

claims.statement: Fairies may be dangerous or benevolent depending on human conduct in stories.
claims.statement_id: Fairy dapat berbahaya atau baik hati tergantung perlakuan manusia dalam cerita.
claims.quote: They are typically capricious, dangerous and vengeful, though may display benevolence so long as great care is taken not to offend them by breaking their curious protocols.

claims.statement: Fairy stories include child abduction and changeling substitution.
claims.statement_id: Cerita fairy memuat penculikan anak dan penggantian dengan changeling.
claims.quote: They carry off children, leaving changeling substitutes, transport men and women into fairyland

claims.statement: In older stories some fairies fly without wings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita lama, sebagian fairy terbang tanpa sayap.
claims.quote: Though some can fly, they do not have wings, but levitate by mounting twigs, bundles of grass or plant stems, wearing a special cap or uttering a set of potent words.

claims.statement: Fairy lore has been studied in Folklore since the late nineteenth century.
claims.statement_id: Cerita fairy telah diteliti dalam jurnal Folklore sejak akhir abad ke-19.
claims.quote: fairy lore has provided a fruitful area of investigation for contributors to the journal Folklore since its founding in the late nineteenth century.

claims.statement: Some Irish and Scottish fairies are described as ordinary human size.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian peri Irlandia dan Skotlandia digambarkan setinggi manusia biasa.
claims.quote: The “people of peace” (Daoine Shie) of Ireland and Scotland are usually of ordinary stature, indeed not to be recognized as varying from mankind except by their proceedings

description.en: A Fängge (plural Fänggen) is a wood sprite or a subtype of wild women in German folklore, found in German-speaking parts of the Alpine Region into more northerly non-Alpine parts of Bavaria (Upper Palatinate). The Fängge has been conceived of strictly as female, a hairy, ugly giantess (counterpart of the moss-grown male giant or wild man). However, the gender demarcation is vague. Also, the spirit when called by the variant name Fankerl or Waldfänken tends to be regarded as a dwarf. They are called Fankel, Fank (var. Fengge; and feminine Fanka, Fanga) in some parts of Austria where they are considered to be "wild folk" of either sex, but less monstrous.

claims.statement: A Fängge (plural Fänggen) is a wood sprite or kind of wild woman in German folklore, found in the German-speaking Alpine region and further north in Bavaria (Upper Palatinate).

claims.statement: The Fankerl is a bearded dwarf with flashy red eyes on the Pfreimd River in Upper Palatinate lore, Bavaria, counted as a type of Fängge.
claims.statement_id: Fankerl adalah kurcaci berjanggut bermata merah menyala yang tinggal di Sungai Pfreimd menurut cerita Oberpfalz (Upper Palatinate), Bayern (Bavaria), dan digolongkan sebagai Fängge.

claims.statement: Per the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps, the Fängge (Fangga) is a giantess as tall as a tree.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita Tirol (Tyrol) dan Alpen Bayern (Bavarian Alps), Fängge (Fangga) adalah raksasa perempuan setinggi pohon.
claims.quote: The Fängge (var. Fangga ) is a giantess as tall as a tree, according to the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps.

claims.statement: The Fänggen (singular Fangga, Fanggin), also Fänken, Fenggen and Fanggen, are legendary beings of southern Germany (Süddeutschland), Austria (Österreich) and South Tyrol (Südtirol); by author, time and place they are giant forest demons, witch figures or tree-bound forest fairies.
claims.statement_id: Fänggen (tunggal Fangga, Fanggin), juga Fänken, Fenggen, dan Fanggen, adalah makhluk legenda di Jerman selatan (Süddeutschland), Austria (Österreich), dan Tirol Selatan (Südtirol); tergantung pengarang, masa, dan tempat mereka digambarkan sebagai setan hutan raksasa, sosok penyihir, atau peri hutan yang terikat pada pohon.
claims.quote: Die Fänggen (Sing.: Fangga; Fanggin), welche auch Fänken, Fenggen und Fanggen genannt werden, sind Wesen und Sagengestalten in Süddeutschland, Österreich und Südtirol. Je nach Autor, Zeit und Ort werden sie entweder als riesenhafte Walddämonen, als Hexengestalten oder auch als baumverbundene Waldfeen beschrieben.

claims.statement: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) describes the Fänggen as huge, hairy all over, with a distorted face, a mouth stretched from ear to ear and black hair hung with tree-beard.
claims.statement_id: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) melukiskan Fänggen sangat besar, berbulu sekujur tubuh, wajah berkerut, mulut terentang dari telinga ke telinga, rambut hitam penuh lumut janggut pohon.
claims.quote: riesengroß, am ganzen Körper behaart, geborstet, das Antlitz verzerrt, der Mund von einem Ohre zum anderen gezogen, das schwarze Haupthaar hängt voll Baumbart

claims.statement: They are said to have secret knowledge, such as the hidden powers of plants, which can be coaxed from them once drunk; most have names like Rauhrinda and Stutzförcha; in legends they are often reduced to bogeys for children or shown as stupid.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon memiliki pengetahuan rahasia, misalnya tentang khasiat tersembunyi tumbuhan, yang bisa dikorek setelah mereka dibuat mabuk; kebanyakan punya nama diri seperti Rauhrinda dan Stutzförcha; dalam legenda mereka sering dijadikan momok anak atau digambarkan bodoh.
claims.quote: Es heißt, dass sie über geheimes Wissen verfügen, wie zum Beispiel jenes über die geheimen Kräfte der Pflanzen, das man ihnen entlocken kann, wenn man sie erst betrunken gemacht hat. Auch sollen die meisten über Eigennamen verfügen, wie zum Beispiel Rauhrinda und Stutzförcha. In Sagen werden sie häufig zum Kinderschreck deklassiert oder als dumm dargestellt.

claims.statement: They appear alone or in groups, but their lives are always bound to a particular forest; if it disappears, say through felling, they disappear too.
claims.statement_id: Mereka muncul sendirian maupun berkelompok, tetapi hidupnya selalu terikat pada hutan tertentu; bila hutan itu hilang, misalnya karena ditebang, mereka pun lenyap.
claims.quote: Sie sollen sowohl solitär, als auch in Gruppen auftreten, wie in den oben beschriebenen Sagen, sind dabei aber stets an einen bestimmten Wald mit ihrem Leben gebunden. Würde besagter Wald verschwinden, etwa durch Abholzung, würden auch sie verschwinden.

claims.statement: Besides giant Fänggen, some legends know small dwarf-like Fängge living in rock clefts and mounds called Fänggenlöcher.
claims.statement_id: Selain Fänggen raksasa, dalam beberapa legenda ada pula Fängge kecil seperti kurcaci yang tinggal di celah batu dan gundukan tanah yang disebut Fänggenlöcher.
claims.quote: Neben den riesenhaften Fänggen existieren in manchen Sagen und Erzählungen auch kleine, zwerghafte Fängge. Diese Winzlinge sollen in Felsenklüften und Erdhügeln, die Fänggenlöcher genannt werden, hausen.

claims.statement: Another trait, surely added with Christianisation, is that the Fänggen, like other pagan figures, can be driven off by the ringing of a church bell.
claims.statement_id: Ciri lain yang pasti baru muncul seiring Kristenisasi: Fänggen, seperti sosok pagan lain, dapat diusir dengan dentang lonceng gereja.
claims.quote: Ein weiteres Merkmal der Fänggen, das sicherlich erst im Zuge der Christianisierung hinzukam, ist, dass man sie, wie auch andere heidnische Gestalten durch das Läuten einer Kirchenglocke vertreiben kann.

claims.statement: Their eyes are dark and coal-black but sometimes glow and flash; their voice is a man's, rough and coarse; they wear aprons of wildcat fur, jackets of tree bark and shaggy fox-skin aprons.
claims.statement_id: Mata mereka gelap sehitam arang tetapi kadang menyala dan memancarkan kilat; suara mereka suara lelaki yang kasar; pakaiannya celemek kulit kucing hutan, jaket kulit kayu, dan celemek bulu rubah.
claims.quote: Die Augen sind dunkel und nachtschwarz wie Kohlen, glühen aber auch zu Zeiten und sprühen Blitze – die Stimme ist Mannesstimme, rauh und ungefüge. Ihre Kleidung sind Schurze von Wildkatzenpelzen, Joppen von Baumrinden und Zottelschurze von Füchsen und anderm Getier.

claims.statement: The small Fängge are often equated with dwarfs and gnomes but, despite their size, are immensely strong; they tame chamois and wolves, drink their milk and even ride them.
claims.statement_id: Fängge kecil sering disamakan dengan kurcaci dan gnome tetapi, meski bertubuh kecil, sangat kuat; mereka menjinakkan chamois dan serigala, meminum susunya, bahkan menungganginya.
claims.quote: Sie werden oft mit den Zwergen, Gnomen und derlei gleichgesetzt, sollen aber, trotz ihrer geringen Körpergröße, über gewaltige Kräfte verfügen. Außerdem heißt es, dass sie Gämse und Wölfe zähmen, deren Milch trinken und sie gar als Reittiere nutzen sollen.

claims.statement: A Tyrolean (Tiroler) legend: in the forest from Nassereit to Stra lived a Fangg as tall as a middling tree, always lurking for people; when she caught little boys she snuffed them up her nose.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Tirol (Tiroler): di hutan antara Nassereit dan Stra tinggal seekor Fangg setinggi pohon sedang yang selalu mengintai manusia, dan bila menangkap anak lelaki kecil, ia mengisapnya ke dalam hidungnya seperti tembakau.
claims.quote: „Im Walde, der von Nassereit nach Stra sich zieht, hauste eine Fangg, welche von der Größe eines mittelmäßigen Baumes war. Sie lauerte stets auf Menschen, und wenn sie kleine Buben zu fassen bekam, so schnupfte sie dieselben in ihre Nase

description.en: Fat Lips (or Fatlips) is the name given to a legendary spirit dwelling in Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland. The spirit was associated with a homeless woman who moved into a vault beneath the ruins of the abbey some time after the 1745 Jacobite rising. The woman claimed that the spirit, "Fatlips," was a little man who tidied the room while she was away, and kept the cell she lived in dry by stamping moisture away from the ground with his heavy iron boots.

claims.statement: Fat Lips is documented as lips fatlips given in regional lore.
claims.statement_id: Fat Lips adalah figur mitologis dalam catatan cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Fat Lips (or Fatlips) is the name given to a legendary spirit dwelling in Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland.

description.en: In Chinese mythology and folklore, Feng (Chinese: 封; pinyin: Fēng; lit. 'mound', 'hump') is an edible monster that resembles a two-eyed lump of meat and magically grows back as fast as it is eaten. Early Chinese texts also referred to this legendary food with the names Shìròu (視肉; 'look like meat'), Ròuzhī (肉芝; 'meat excrescence'), and Tàisuì (太歲; "great year; Jupiter"). Ròulíngzhī (肉靈芝; "meaty Lingzhi mushroom") is a modern name popularized by Chinese news media reporting on purported discoveries of Feng throughout China.

description.en: A fetch is a supernatural double or an apparition of a living person. The sighting of a fetch is regarded as an inevitable omen, usually for impending death to oneself, or a loved one.

description.en: In Orkney folklore, Finfolk (sometimes Finnfolk) are sorcerous shapeshifters of the sea, the dark mysterious race from Finfolkaheem who regularly make an amphibious journey from the depths of the Finfolk ocean home to the Orkney Islands. They wade, swim or sometimes row upon the Orkney shores in the spring and summer months, searching for human captives. The Finfolk (both Finman and Finwife) kidnap unsuspecting fishermen, or frolicking youth, near the shore and force them into lifelong servitude as a spouse.

description.en: Firedrakes in English folklore (also written uncompounded: fire-drake; Old English: fyrdraca) are obscure, but still appear in various old stories, poetry, and even Shakespeare. Firedrakes are dragon-sightings stemming from shooting stars and will-o'-the-wisps, said to appear as dragon-shaped fireballs or sparking streaks of fire in the sky, and the term also appears as a synonym for the above, including "fiery dragon" and "fiery meteor". While not unique to English folklore, the firedrake have often been thought to be the Devil himself in dragon shape.

description.en: The Floçka also known as the "Gërzheta" is a nymph-like creature from Albanian paganism. They are described as inhabiting the lands near bodies of water such as lakes and islands in hidden parts of the mountains. The Floçka are said to have immense beauty.

description.en: The Four Holy Beasts (Chinese: 四靈、四聖獸、or 四大神獸) are Chinese astronomical and cultural Four Benevolent Animals that are spread in the East Asian cultural sphere. description.en: Freybug is a monstrous Black Dog that is stated to come from medieval English folklore, specifically from Norfolk. Like most supernatural black dogs, it was roughly the size of a calf, and wandered country roads terrifying travelers. The English martyr Laurence Saunders mentioned Fray-bugs in his letters to his wife in 1555. The word Fray-bug is defined by the Oxford English Dictionary as “an object of fear; a bogy, spectre.” The similar word “fray-boggart” was a word for a scarecrow. Popular Antiquities of Great Britain, by John Brand, referenced Saunders' letters and suggested that the Fray-bug was a Black Dog similar to the Barghest. Carol Rose seems to have drawn on Brand’s work for her description of the Freybug.

description.en: Gagana is a miraculous bird with an iron beak and copper claws featured in Russian folklore. She is said to live on the Buyan Island. The bird is often mentioned in incantations. It is also said this bird guards the Alatyr, alongside Garafena the snake. Gagana knows how to conjure and work miracles and, if she is asked correctly, can help a person. This bird is also the only one capable of giving the milk of the birds.

description.en: In Scottish folklore, the Galloway Puma is a "phantom cat" said to dwell in Dumfries and Galloway, in south-west Scotland. The rumours of a big cat in Galloway began in the late 1990s, when Canadian tourists claimed to have seen an animal which resembled a cougar near Kirroughtree, south-east of Newton Stewart. The tourists apparently saw the animal while returning from a nature walk in the Galloway Forest. It was also allegedly sighted by locals in Newton Stewart in 1999. After this, many people, specifically farmers and Forestry Commission workers, claimed to have seen a big black cat throughout the region, but mainly in the Machars area. In June 2001, a young lady walking her dog near Newton Stewart golf course, which lies on the edge of Galloway Forest, was left startled and shaken when what she described as a "large black cat, bigger than an alsatian", sprung out at her on the path on which she was walking. She further claims that the animal ran away after her dog began barking and growling at it.

description.en: According to the folklore of Trinidad and Tobago, Gang Gang Sarah is an African witch who was blown off course to Tobago on a strong wind and landed in the village of Les Coteaux. She chose to stay for a while to search for her family, but when at last she decided to go home found that she had lost the power of flight because she had eaten salt during her stay in Golden Lane, Tobago. While in Tobago, she became the wife of a man named Tom. She lived to a great age and is remembered for her kindness.

description.en: The Ghillie Dhu or Gille Dubh (Scottish Gaelic pronunciation: [ˈkʲiʎə ˈt̪u]) is a solitary male fairy described in Scottish folklore. He was said to be dark-haired, and clothed in leaves and moss, from which the ghillie suit got its name. He appears primarily in accounts from the late 18th century, living in a birch wood in the north-west Highlands of Scotland. He was said to fiercely protect the forest from outsiders, but with accounts of him treating children with kindness.

description.en: Gnome king Kyrië (Dutch: Kabouterkoning Kyrië, pronounced [kaːˈbʌutərˌkoːnɪŋ ˈkiːrijə]) is, according to local folklore, the leader of the legendary gnomes (kabouters) who lived in the Campine region of the province of North Brabant, the Netherlands. These gnomes had their base in the village of Hoogeloon, from which they journeyed into neighboring lands. According to tradition the gnome king Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ("gnome mountain"), also known as Duivelsberg ("devil's mountain"), a tumulus located in the Koebosch forest, slightly northeast of Hoogeloon.

description.en: In a broad sense, Goryō (御霊; Japanese: [ɡoɾʲoː]) is an honorific for a spirit, especially one that causes hauntings, and the term is used as a synonym for onryō (怨霊, vengeful Japanese ghosts). In a narrower sense, it refers to a noble or accomplished person who lost a political power struggle or died prematurely from an epidemic or other disease, becoming an onryō that brings pestilence or famine and is later enshrined as a kami in Shinto shrines. For example, the "Sandai Jitsuroku" (a historical Japanese document) mentions that six Shinto shrines were dedicated to the worship of goryō, which were the spirits of those who died from non-natural causes. Later on, two more shrines were added, bringing the total to eight. Goryō Shinko (御霊信仰, Belief in goryō) refers to the belief that the onryō of people who have died unfortunate deaths cause hauntings and disasters, and the belief that they are enshrined as kami to appease them.

description.en: Grant, or Gyant, is a creature of English folklore described in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury. Gervase describes it as a "kind of demon" resembling "a yearling colt, prancing on its hind-legs, with sparkling eyes", which runs through towns as a warning of fire. Gervase's account is the only known medieval source to name the creature. Francis Young links the Grant to a wider motif in Britain and Ireland of horse-like bogies encountered on isolated roads by travellers, such as the púca, kelpie, or shagfoal, and suggests that the idea of such beings as warnings of fire is not prominent in later folklore. Joseph Pentangelo instead argues that it was probably a hare, and that the description in the Otia Imperialia may reflect embellishment by Gervase or his informant. He bases this interpretation on later folk beliefs in which a hare running through a village street was treated as a warning of fire, and on the similarities in form. Earlier writers proposed other identifications. Felix Liebrecht compared the Grant with Grendel and with the demons in the legend of St Guthlac and argued that it was a water spirit. Thomas Keightley and Jacob Grimm likewise linked it to Grendel, largely through name similarity. A 1708 edition of John Cowell's Law Dictionary suggested comparing the grant with the Barguest, a death-omen in northern English folklore, though Pentangelo notes that beyond a few general similarities the creatures have little in common.

description.en: A groac'h (Breton for "fairy", "witch" or "crone", pl. groagez) is a kind of Breton water-fairy. Seen in various forms, often by night, many are old, similar to ogres and witches, sometimes with walrus teeth. Supposed to live in caverns, under the beach and under the sea, the groac'h has power over the forces of nature and can change its shape. It is mainly known as a malevolent figure, largely because of Émile Souvestre's story La Groac'h de l'île du Lok, in which the fairy seduces men, changes them into fish and serves them as meals to her guests, on one of the Glénan Islands. Other tales present them as old solitary fairies who can overwhelm with gifts the humans who visit them. Several place-names of Lower Brittany are connected with the groac'h, especially the names of some megaliths in Côtes-d'Armor, as well as the island of Groix in Morbihan and the lighthouse of La Vieille. The origin of those fairies that belong to the archetype of "the crone" is to be found in the ancient female divinities demonized by Christianity. The influence of Breton writers in the 19th century brought them closer to the classical fairy figure. The groac'h has several times appeared in recent literary works, such as Nicolas Bréhal's La Pâleur et le Sang (1983).

description.en: Guhyaka(s) (गुह्यक, literally "hidden ones") is a class of supernatural beings in Hindu mythology. Like Yakshas (nature-spirits), they are often described as attendants of Kubera, the keeper of wealth, and protect his hidden treasures. Guhyakas are believed to live in mountain caves; thus their name, "hidden ones". As lord of Guhyakas, Kubera is called "Guhyakadhipati".

description.en: In a Māori tradition ascribed by John White to the Ngāti Hau tribe, Hāhau-whenua is the name of the great fish caught by Māui which became the North Island of New Zealand (In Māori the North Island is known as Te ika-a-Māui, the fish of Māui).
