claims.statement_id: Burung Gereja Ulm (Ulmer Spatz) adalah tengara dan lambang kota Ulm di Jerman (German), berupa patung burung di atas Katedral Ulm (Ulm Minster), gereja tertinggi kedua di dunia.
claims.quote: The Ulm Sparrow (Ger. Ulmer Spatz) is a landmark in, and symbol of, the German city of Ulm. The landmark is a statue of a bird that sits atop the Ulm Minster, the second-tallest church in the world.

claims.statement: Legend says the people of Ulm carted a huge beam for building the minster (Münsters) but could not get it through the city gate; about to tear the gate down, they saw a sparrow carrying a twig for its nest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, warga Ulm membawa balok sangat besar untuk membangun katedral (Münsters) tetapi tak bisa memasukkannya lewat gerbang kota; saat hendak merobohkan gerbang, mereka melihat burung gereja membawa ranting untuk sarangnya.
claims.quote: Der Sage nach sollen die Ulmer beim Bau des Münsters einen besonders großen Balken angekarrt haben. Sie schafften es aber nicht, ihn durch das Stadttor zu bringen. Als sie kurz davor waren, das Tor einzureißen, sahen sie einen Spatzen, der einen Zweig im Schnabel trug, um diesen in sein Nest einzubauen.

claims.statement: The sparrow turned the twig lengthwise before building it in; the Ulmers then saw the light and laid the beam lengthwise on their cart rather than across as before; the Ulmer Spatz is a landmark (Wahrzeichen) of Ulm.
claims.statement_id: Burung gereja itu memutar rantingnya memanjang sebelum menyusunnya; warga Ulm pun tersadar dan meletakkan balok memanjang di gerobak, bukan melintang seperti sebelumnya; Ulmer Spatz adalah lambang (Wahrzeichen) Ulm.
claims.quote: Dieser Spatz drehte den Zweig vor dem Einbau längsseits. Da ging dann wohl auch den Ulmern ein Licht auf und sie legten den Balken der Länge nach auf ihren Karren und nicht quer, wie bisher.

claims.statement: This humorous legend is traceable from the second quarter of the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Legenda jenaka ini dapat dilacak sejak perempat kedua abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Diese humoristische Sage ist seit dem zweiten Viertel des 19. Jahrhunderts nachweisbar.

claims.statement: It belongs to a widespread cycle of tales about logs and beams carried crosswise, solved by watching a bird (sparrow, stork, jackdaw) build its nest; in 1872 Eduard Mauch called it a 'falsification of history' (Geschichtsfälschung).
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini termasuk kelompok kisah yang tersebar luas tentang batang kayu dan balok yang diangkut melintang, dipecahkan dengan mengamati burung (burung gereja, bangau, gagak) membangun sarang; pada 1872 Eduard Mauch menyebutnya "pemalsuan sejarah" (Geschichtsfälschung).
claims.quote: Sie gehört zu dem weit verbreiteten Sagenkreis um kreuzweis statt längsseits transportierte Baumstämme und Holzbalken, wobei die Lösung des Problems durch die Beobachtung eines Vogels (Sperling, Storch, Dohle etc.) beim Nestbau gewonnen wurde. Schon 1872 bezeichnete Eduard Mauch die Sage als eine „Geschichtsfälschung“

claims.statement: In 1842 Carl Hertzog published his poem 'Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage'.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1842 Carl Hertzog menerbitkan puisinya "Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage".
claims.quote: Bereits 1842 veröffentlichte Carl Hertzog (1810–nach 1874) sein Gedicht „Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage“.

claims.statement: The figure on the nave of Ulm Minster was donated by wealthy citizens; it is not a sparrow but a dove with an olive branch, as in the biblical story of Noah's Ark, and small relative to the building, easily seen only from the tower.
claims.statement_id: Sosok di atap nave Katedral Ulm (Ulm Minster) disumbangkan warga kaya; ia bukan burung gereja melainkan merpati pembawa ranting zaitun seperti kisah Bahtera Nuh (Noah's Ark), dan tampak kecil dibanding bangunannya, hanya mudah terlihat dari menara.
claims.quote: The figure on the nave of Ulm Minster was donated by wealthy citizens. It is not a sparrow, but a dove carrying an olive branch in its beak, as in the biblical story of Noah's Ark. It is small in relation to the building, and only easily visible from the tower.

claims.statement: The original Ulmer Spatz of 1858 from the minster roof (Münsterdach) is now in a display case near the entrance of Ulm Minster (Ulmer Münster).
claims.statement_id: Ulmer Spatz asli tahun 1858 dari atap katedral (Münsterdach) kini berada dalam lemari kaca di dekat pintu masuk Katedral Ulm (Ulmer Münster).
claims.quote: „Ulmer Spatz“: das Original aus dem Jahr 1858 vom Münsterdach befindet sich heute im Ulmer Münster nahe dem Eingang in einer Vitrine

description.en: The unclean dead, according to Slavic folklore, are those who died an unnatural death and did not find peace after death. They were believed to return to the world of the living and continue their existence on earth as malevolent mythical beings. In Russian ethnography, the term zalozhnye pokoiniki (Russian: заложные покойники) is also used to describe these beings; it was introduced into scholarly discourse in the early 20th century by ethnographer Dmitry Zelenin, as the "unclean dead" had no single name common across all Slavic traditions. It was believed that the soul of a so-called "restless" (Russian: неупокоенный) dead could not pass on to the afterlife and therefore wandered the earth. According to Slavic folklore, such dead could turn into malevolent spirits.

claims.statement: According to Slavic folklore, the unclean dead are those who died an unnatural death and found no peace afterwards; they were believed to return to the world of the living and go on existing on earth as malevolent mythical beings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Slavia, arwah najis adalah orang yang mati secara tidak wajar dan tidak menemukan kedamaian setelah mati; mereka dipercaya kembali ke dunia orang hidup dan melanjutkan keberadaan di bumi sebagai makhluk mitos yang jahat.
claims.quote: The unclean dead, according to Slavic folklore, are those who died an unnatural death and did not find peace after death. They were believed to return to the world of the living and continue their existence on earth as malevolent mythical beings.

claims.statement: Russian ethnography also uses the term zalozhnye pokoiniki (заложные покойники), introduced into scholarship in the early 20th century by the ethnographer Dmitry Zelenin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam etnografi Rusia dipakai pula istilah zalozhnye pokoiniki (заложные покойники), yang diperkenalkan ke dunia ilmiah pada awal abad ke-20 oleh etnografer Dmitry Zelenin.
claims.quote: In Russian ethnography, the term zalozhnye pokoiniki (Russian: заложные покойники ) is also used

claims.statement: It was believed that the soul of a "restless" dead person could not pass into the afterlife and so wandered the earth, and that such dead could turn into malevolent spirits.
claims.statement_id: Diyakini bahwa jiwa orang mati yang "tak tenang" tidak bisa pergi ke alam baka sehingga mengembara di bumi, dan orang mati semacam itu bisa berubah menjadi roh jahat.
claims.quote: It was believed that the soul of a so-called "restless" (Russian: неупокоенный ) dead could not pass on to the afterlife and therefore wandered the earth. According to Slavic folklore, such dead could turn into malevolent spirits.

claims.statement: They were buried outside church grounds, at places such as crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps or ravines, because they were believed to be "cursed by their parents, and the earth would not receive them".
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikuburkan di luar lingkungan gereja, misalnya di persimpangan jalan, batas ladang, hutan, rawa, atau jurang, karena dipercaya "dikutuk orang tua mereka dan bumi tidak mau menerima mereka".
claims.quote: Rather, they were buried outside the territory of a church, in places such as at crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps, or ravines, since it was believed that they were "cursed by their parents and the earth would not receive them."

claims.statement: "Zalozhny dead" were typically those who died violently, suicides, those who died of drink, the drowned, unbaptised children, sorcerers and witches.
claims.statement_id: Yang biasanya dianggap "zalozhny" adalah orang yang mati karena kekerasan, bunuh diri, mati karena mabuk, mati tenggelam, anak yang belum dibaptis, dukun, dan penyihir.
claims.quote: "Zalozhny dead" were typically considered to be those who died violently, suicides, drunken deaths, drowning victims, unbaptized children, sorcerers, and witches.

claims.statement: Zelenin linked the origin of the word "zalozhny" to the burial method: the body was laid face down in the coffin and the grave sealed with stones and branches.
claims.statement_id: Zelenin mengaitkan asal kata "zalozhny" dengan cara penguburannya: jasad diletakkan telungkup di dalam peti dan kuburnya ditutup dengan batu dan ranting.
claims.quote: He linked the origin of the word “zalozhny” to the burial method itself: the body was placed face down in the coffin, and the grave was sealed with stones and branches

claims.statement: The Russian article describes заложные покойники as people who, in Slavic belief, died an unnatural death and found no rest after death.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rusia menyebut заложные покойники sebagai orang yang menurut kepercayaan Slavia mati tidak wajar dan tidak mendapat ketenangan setelah mati.
claims.quote: по славянским верованиям, умершие неестественной смертью люди, не получившие после смерти успокоения.

claims.statement: In Simbirsk Governorate it was believed that during a drought one had to find a drunkard whom the earth would not accept, dig him up and throw him into a swamp so that rain would come.
claims.statement_id: Di Kegubernuran Simbirsk ada kepercayaan bahwa saat kemarau orang harus menemukan pemabuk yang tidak diterima bumi, menggalinya, dan membuangnya ke rawa agar hujan turun.
claims.quote: В Симбирской губернии существовало поверье, что во время засухи «надо непременно найти опойца, которого не принимает земля, поэтому его надо вырыть из земли и кинуть в болото, чтобы пошёл дождь».

claims.statement: There is a legend of Baturka, believed to be very greedy, so that passers-by had to leave an offering or he might bring disease on them and their livestock.
claims.statement_id: Ada legenda tentang Baturka yang dipercaya sangat rakus, sehingga orang yang lewat harus meninggalkan persembahan; kalau tidak, ia bisa mendatangkan penyakit kepada mereka dan ternaknya.
claims.quote: Известна, например, легенда о Батурке, который по поверью был очень жадным, поэтому, чтобы утолить его алчность, проходящие мимо люди должны были сделать подношение, иначе он мог нагнать на них и их скот болезнь.

claims.statement: In Belarus places of violent death were considered unclean, and passers-by threw stones, branches, a tuft of straw or a handful of earth onto them, "or else the dead man will chase them for a long time".
claims.statement_id: Di Belarus tempat kematian karena kekerasan dianggap najis, dan orang yang lewat melemparkan batu, ranting, seikat jerami, atau segenggam tanah ke tempat itu agar si mati tidak mengejar mereka.
claims.quote: В Беларуси места насильственной смерти считались нечистыми, и проходящие мимо люди на такие места бросали камни, ветки деревьев, клок соломы или горсть земли («иначе умерший будет за ними долго гнаться»).

claims.statement: Dmitry Zelenin equated the "zalozhny" dead with rusalkas.
claims.statement_id: Dmitry Zelenin menyamakan arwah "zalozhny" dengan rusalka.
claims.quote: Дмитрий Зеленин ставил знак равенства между «заложными» покойниками и русалками.

claims.statement: The upyr is a "zalozhny" dead person, most often a dead sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Upyr adalah arwah "zalozhny", paling sering seorang dukun yang telah mati.
claims.quote: Упырь — «заложный» покойник, чаще всего умерший колдун.

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article calls Заложні мерці a collective name for beings who, in Slavic and especially Ukrainian folk belief, were people who died an unnatural death or lived a bad, unworthy life, so their souls cannot pass to the other world.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebut Заложні мерці sebagai nama kolektif makhluk yang menurut kepercayaan rakyat Slavia, termasuk Ukraina, dulunya manusia yang mati tidak wajar atau hidup buruk dan tak layak, sehingga jiwanya tidak bisa pergi ke alam baka.
claims.quote: збірна назва істот, що за слов'янськими, зокрема українськими, народними повір'ями були людьми, котрі померли неприродною смертю, або які жили поганим, негідним життям, і тому їхні душі не можуть піти до потойбічного світу.

claims.statement: In many places it was believed that the earth does not accept the unclean dead: their bodies do not decay and the earth itself pushes them to the surface.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak tempat dipercaya bahwa bumi tidak menerima arwah najis: jasad mereka tidak membusuk dan bumi sendiri mendorong mereka ke permukaan.
claims.quote: В багатьох місцях вірили, що земля не приймає заложних мерців, їхні тіла не розкладаються і земля сама виштовхує їх на поверхню.

claims.statement: To stop such dead from visiting the living, a bundle of blessed poppy seed was placed in their graves, and people sprinkled their own houses with blessed poppy or flax.
claims.statement_id: Agar arwah semacam itu tidak bisa mendatangi orang hidup, ke dalam kuburnya diletakkan bungkusan biji poppy yang telah diberkati, dan rumah sendiri ditaburi poppy atau rami yang diberkati.
claims.quote: Аби позбавити таких покійників здатності відвідувати живих людей, в їхні могили клали вузлик свяченого маку-видюку. Власні ж хати обсипали свяченим маком або льоном.

description.id: Uraeus (; jamak Uraei atau Uraeuses; dari kata Yunani οὐραῖος, ouraîos, "di ekornya"; dari kata Mesir jʿr.t (iaret)) adalah sebuah bentuk dari kobra Mesir yang dipakai sebagai simbol kedaulatan, keningratan, deitas dan otoritas ilahi di Mesir kuno.
description.en: The uraeus () or ouraeus (Ancient Greek: Οὐραῖος, Greek pronunciation: [οὐραῖος] ; Egyptian: jꜥrt, "rearing cobra", plural: uraei) is the stylized, upright form of an Egyptian cobra, used as a symbol of sovereignty, royalty, deity and divine authority in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: The uraeus is an upright cobra representation in Egyptian tradition symbolizing royal power and divine authority.
claims.statement_id: Uraeus adalah gambaran kobra tegak dalam tradisi Mesir yang melambangkan kekuasaan kerajaan dan otoritas ilahi.
claims.quote: is the stylized, upright form of an Egyptian cobra, used as a symbol of sovereignty, royalty, deity and divine authority in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: The uraeus represents the goddess Wadjet.
claims.statement_id: Uraeus merupakan lambang dewi Wadjet.
claims.quote: The uraeus is a symbol for the goddess Wadjet.

claims.statement: Its use on the crown signifies Wadjet’s protection of the pharaoh.
claims.statement_id: Pemakaiannya pada mahkota menandakan perlindungan Wadjet terhadap firaun.
claims.quote: this indicated Wadjet's protection and reinforced the pharaoh's claim over the land.

claims.statement: Nekhbet and Wadjet become the Two Ladies protecting unified Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Nekhbet dan Wadjet menjadi Dua Nyonya yang menjaga Mesir bersatu.
claims.quote: Together, they were known as the Nebty or the Two Ladies, who became the joint protectors and patrons of the unified Egypt.

claims.statement: Wadjet, represented by the uraeus, is described as Ra’s daughter and a figure in Eye of Ra stories.
claims.statement_id: Wadjet, yang dilambangkan uraeus, disebut putri Ra dan tokoh kisah Mata Ra.
claims.quote: She was the daughter of Ra and one of the goddesses featured in stories about the Eye of Ra.

claims.statement: The accompanying encyclopedia calls the uraeus the king’s insignia in the form of Wadjet’s rearing cobra.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia pendamping menyebut uraeus sebagai insignia raja berupa kobra Wadjet yang terangkat.
claims.quote: represented as the rearing cobra which became the king's insignia (the uraeus).

description.en: The Utah Lake Monster is a legendary creature reportedly inhabiting Utah Lake in Utah County. The legend may have roots in local Ute traditions regarding aquatic beings known as Pawapicts (or "Water Babies"), and continued through sightings reported by 19th-century settlers.

claims.statement: The Utah Lake Monster is a legendary creature reportedly inhabiting Utah Lake in Utah County.
claims.statement_id: Utah Lake Monster adalah makhluk legendaris yang dilaporkan menghuni Utah Lake di Utah County.
claims.quote: The Utah Lake Monster is a legendary creature reportedly inhabiting Utah Lake in Utah County.

claims.statement: The legend may have roots in local Ute traditions regarding aquatic beings known as Pawapicts (or Water Babies).
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini berakar dari tradisi suku Ute tentang makhluk air yang disebut Pawapicts (Water Babies).
claims.quote: The legend may have roots in local Ute traditions regarding aquatic beings known as Pawapicts (or "Water Babies"), and continued through sightings reported by 19th-century settlers.

description.en: A Vadleány is a spiritual being from Central European (Hungarian) folklore. Similar to nymphs or dryads, Vadleány have extremely long hair, long fingernails, and are completely nude. According to the Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, they seduce wanderers and steal their strength. The name translates to "wild girl". When one is present, the trees make a rustling sound. She could reputedly be caught by placing one boot where she habitually walked; out of curiosity she would try to put both feet in it and be caught.

claims.statement: The Vadleány is a spirit being of Central European (Hungarian) folklore; like nymphs or dryads, she has extremely long hair and long fingernails and is completely nude.
claims.statement_id: Vadleány adalah makhluk roh dari cerita rakyat Eropa Tengah (Hungaria); mirip nimfa atau driad, ia berambut sangat panjang, berkuku panjang, dan sepenuhnya telanjang.
claims.quote: A Vadleány is a spiritual being from Central European (Hungarian) folklore. Similar to nymphs or dryads, Vadleány have extremely long hair, long fingernails, and are completely nude.

claims.statement: According to the Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, vadleány seduce wanderers and steal their strength; the name means "wild girl".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, vadleány menggoda para pengembara dan mencuri kekuatan mereka; namanya berarti "gadis liar".
claims.quote: According to the Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, they seduce wanderers and steal their strength. The name translates to "wild girl".

claims.statement: When a vadleány is present, the trees rustle.
claims.statement_id: Ketika seorang vadleány hadir, pepohonan berdesir.
claims.quote: When one is present, the trees make a rustling sound.

claims.statement: The Hungarian article calls the vadleány a supernatural being of Central European, in particular Hungarian, folklore: a forest being who seduces travellers and steals their strength.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Hungaria menyebut vadleány sebagai makhluk gaib dalam folklor Eropa Tengah, khususnya Hungaria: makhluk hutan yang menggoda para pelancong dan mencuri kekuatan mereka.
claims.quote: A vadleány egy természetfeletti lény a közép-európai (azon belül a magyar) folklórban. Erdei lény, aki elcsábítja az utazókat, és ellopja az erejüket.

claims.statement: The Hungarians of Lápos (láposi magyarok) also knew the vadleány: she goes naked (meztelenül jár), her face is beautiful, but her body is covered with hair reaching to the ground.
claims.statement_id: Orang Hungaria di Lápos (láposi magyarok) juga mengenal vadleány: ia berjalan telanjang, wajahnya cantik, tetapi tubuhnya tertutup bulu yang menjuntai sampai ke tanah.
claims.quote: A vadleányt ismerték a láposi magyarok is: meztelenül jár, az arca szép, a testét azonban földig érő szőr fedi.

claims.statement: If angered she raises a wind that breaks trees and scatters the shepherd's hut; according to the people of Domokos she could be caught by setting out one boot of a pair where she usually walked.
claims.statement_id: Jika dibuat marah, ia menimbulkan angin yang mematahkan pohon dan memorakporandakan pondok gembala; menurut orang Domokos, ia bisa ditangkap dengan meletakkan sebelah sepatu bot di jalur yang biasa dilaluinya.
claims.quote: Ha felbosszantják, olyan szelet csinál, hogy fákat tör ki, széthányja a pásztor kalibáját. A domokosiak szerint meg lehetett fogni: amerre járni szokott, fél pár csizmát kellett kitenni.

claims.statement: The Hungarians of Mezőség and Székelyföld also knew this figure, calling her erdei leány (forest girl), éneklő kisasszony (singing maiden) and víg leány (merry girl).
claims.statement_id: Orang Hungaria di Mezőség dan Székelyföld juga mengenal gambaran ini dan menyebutnya erdei leány (gadis hutan), éneklő kisasszony (nona penyanyi), dan víg leány (gadis riang).
claims.quote: A képzetet ismerték a mezőségi és székelyföldi magyarok is: erdei leánynak, éneklő kisasszonynak, víg leánynak emlegették.

claims.statement: Out of curiosity she tried it on but put both feet in, and so could not run away.
claims.statement_id: Karena penasaran ia mencobanya, tetapi memasukkan kedua kakinya sehingga tidak bisa lari.
claims.quote: Kíváncsiságában felpróbálta, de mindkét lábát beledugta, így aztán nem futhatott el.

description.id: Wamana (Dewanagari: वामन ; ,IAST: Vāmana, वामन ) adalah salah satu awatara (penjelmaan) Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, yang berwujud pendeta kerdil, lahir pada masa Tretayuga sebagai putra Dewi Aditi dan Resi Kasyapa. Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana dengan raga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Wamana kadang-kadang dikenal juga dengan sebutan Upendra (Dewanagari: उपेन्द्र; ,IAST: Upendra, उपेन्द्र) yang berarti "adik Indra". Dia memiliki julukan Triwikrama (Dewanagari: त्रिविक्रम; ,IAST: Trivikrama,; arti: "tiga langkah") karena langkah kakinya dapat memijak bumi, patala (dunia bawah), dan swarga (kahyangan) sekaligus. Menurut keyakinan Hindu, Wisnu turun ke dunia pada zaman Tretayuga untuk menegakkan kebenaran dan memberi pelajaran kepada Raja Bali (Mahabali), seorang asura, cucu dari Prahlada. Dalam sastra Hindu dikisahkan bahwa Raja Bali (Mahabali) telah merebut swarga dari kekuasaan Dewa Indra sehingga itu Wisnu selaku dewa pemelihara semesta turun tangan dan menjelma ke dunia, memberi hukuman pada Raja Bali.
description.en: Vamana (Sanskrit: वामन, lit. 'Dwarf', IAST: Vāmana), also known as Trivikrama (lit. 'three steps'), Urukrama (lit. 'far-stepping'), Upendra (lit. 'Indra’s younger brother/Superior to Indra'), Dadhivamana (Sanskrit: दधिवामन, lit. 'milk-dwarf', IAST: Dadhivāmana), Ulagalanthan (lit. 'the one who measured the world) and Balibandhana (lit. 'binder or killer of Bali'), is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps to restore the cosmic order and push Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest among the adityas, the sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

claims.statement: Vamana is the fifth avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu, the first Dashavatara of the Treta Yuga after Narasimha, who in the Vedas and Puranas takes back the three worlds (Trailokya) from Mahabali with three steps.
claims.statement_id: Vamana adalah awatara kelima dewa Hindu Vishnu (Wisnu), Dashavatara pertama di Treta Yuga sesudah Narasimha, yang dalam Weda (Vedas) dan Purana merebut tiga dunia (Trailokya) dari Mahabali dengan tiga langkah (three steps).
claims.quote: is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps

claims.statement: Vāmana (Sanskrit वामन) means dwarf, small or short in stature.
claims.statement_id: Vāmana (Sanskerta, Sanskrit वामन) berarti kerdil (dwarf), kecil, atau pendek.
claims.quote: 'Vāmana' (Sanskrit वामन) means 'dwarf', 'small' or 'small or short in stature'.

claims.statement: He restores cosmic order and pushes Mahabali into the netherworld; he is the youngest of the adityas, sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

claims.statement: Wamana is an avatar of the god Vishnu (Wisnu) in Hinduism, a dwarf priest (pendeta kerdil), son of Aditi and Kasyapa in the Tretayuga.

claims.statement: Wamana's story in the Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana and other Mahapuranas: he came to King Bali's (Raja Bali) palace when Bali invited brahmins for gifts, though Sukracarya had warned Bali.

Menurut cerita dalam kitab, Wamana sebagai brahmana cilik datang ke istana Raja Bali karena pada saat itu Raja Bali mengundang seluruh brahmana untuk diberikan hadiah. Ia sudah dinasihati oleh Sukracarya (Guru Sukra)

claims.statement: The little brahmin asked for land of three strides; King Bali (Raja Bali) granted it, and the brahmin grew until he strode over heaven (surga) and earth (bumi) at once.

claims.quote: brahmana kecil itu meminta tanah seluas tiga jengkal yang diukur dengan langkah kakinya. Raja Bali pun takabur dan melupakan nasihat Sukracarya, dan menyuruh brahmana kecil itu melangkah. Pada waktu itu juga, brahmana tersebut membesar dan terus membesar. claims.statement: His first step trod swarga, the second the earth (bumi), and for the third Bali offered his head (kepalanya).

claims.statement: The epithet Trivikrama means three steps, referring to Vishnu's three strides in the Rigveda.

description.en: Vardøger, also known as vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor in Scandinavian folklore. Stories typically include instances that are nearly déjà vu in substance, but in reverse, where a spirit with the subject's footsteps, voice, scent, or appearance and overall demeanor precedes them in a location or activity, resulting in witnesses believing they have seen or heard the actual person before the person physically arrives. This bears a subtle difference from a doppelgänger, with a less sinister connotation. It has been likened to being a phantom double, or form of bilocation. In Finnish folklore, the concept is known as etiäinen. Originally, vardøger was considered a fylgja and/or vǫrð, a sort of guardian spirit. Thus, a vardøger is the representation of a human's inner essence, which manifests as an animal that most closely resembles the personality of the human.

This bears a subtle difference from a doppelgänger, with a less sinister connotation. It has been likened to being a phantom double, or form of bilocation. In Finnish folklore, the concept is known as etiäinen.

claims.statement: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word meaning 'premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives', from Old Norse varðhygi, of vǫrð ('guard') and hugr ('mind, will, spirit'); in Sweden the same concept is called vård.

claims.quote: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word defined as ‘‘premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives’’. ... The word vardøger is from Old Norse varðhygi, consisting of the elements vǫrð, "care taker, guard, watchman" (akin to "warden") and hugr, 'the mind, will, thought, spirit'. The same concept exists in Sweden but under the name of vård

claims.statement: According to Norwegian folklore, seeing a vardøger means you are crossing someone's path, and often only that the person is on the way.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Norwegia, melihat vardøger berarti kau berpapasan di jalan seseorang, dan sering hanya berarti orang itu sedang dalam perjalanan.
claims.quote: Si ves un vardøger, según el folclore noruego, eso significa que te estas cruzando en el camino de una persona. A menudo solo quiere decir que esa persona de la cual has visto su vardøger está en camino.

claims.statement: Originally a vardøger was considered a fylgja, a kind of guardian spirit of that person.
claims.statement_id: Semula, vardøger dianggap sebuah fylgja, sejenis roh pelindung orang itu.
claims.quote: originalmente, un vardøger era considerado un fylgja, una especie de espíritu guardián de esa persona.

claims.statement: Since the vardøger is a kind of guardian spirit, people who have one are usually called good people protected by a kindly spirit; in short, the vardøger is the counterpart of a doppelgänger.
claims.statement_id: Karena vardøger sejenis roh pelindung, orang yang memilikinya biasa disebut orang baik yang dilindungi roh baik; singkatnya vardøger adalah lawan doppelgänger.
claims.quote: Debido a que el vardøger es un tipo de espíritu guardián, se suele decir de aquellos que tienen un vardøger que son buenas personas, ya que un espíritu benéfico les protege. En resumen, podríamos decir que un vardøger es la contraparte de un doppelgänger.

description.en: The Vegetable Man, also known as the Veggie Man, is a humanoid creature in West Virginia folklore, reportedly seen in Grant Town, West Virginia, in 1968 by local resident Jennings Frederick. The cryptid was first described in print by known hoaxer, Gray Barker in a 1976 newsletter, which characterized it as a thin, plant-like creature with yellow eyes, pointed ears, and fingers ending in needle-like suction cups. No evidence of the alleged sighting has been documented and there have been no subsequent sightings of the creature.

description.en: The Vināyakas were a group of four troublesome demons who created obstacles and difficulties in Hindu mythology, but who were easily propitiated. One theory of the origin of Ganesha is that he gradually came to prominence in connection with the Vināyakas. In Puranic literature of a much later period the group of four Vināyakas was merged into one definite god named Vināyaka whom Rudra appointed as the "Leader of the Ganas" (Ganapati). This Vināyaka-Ganapati is associated with another god called Dantin, "the one with the tusk," who is said to possess a twisted trunk (vakratuṇḍa) and who holds a corn-sheaf, a sugar cane, and a club. This description of Dantin is so characteristic of the Puranic Ganapati that Heras says "we cannot resist to accept his full identification with this Vedic Dantin." The name Vināyaka is a common name for Ganesha both in the Purāṇas and in Buddhist Tantras. In the Smrti of Yājñavalkya, written in the 6th century, Vināyaka is definitely mentioned as a demon who had been exalted to the rank of a deva. He is clearly described as elephant-headed by the 8th century.

description.en: A vittra (plural: vittror) is a type of wight (a term for supernatural beings) from northern Sweden. They were associated with herding, either cattle or reindeer; they were believed to live normally among humans and only revealed a supernatural nature if their livestock were mistreated. Like the hulder and the skogsrå, the vittra is also associated with longing and desire. The vittra appears as a beautiful, female wight who seduces men in the forest.

claims.statement: Vittra or vitter is a side form of vätte and denotes a mythical people in the folk belief of northern Nordic fäbod culture, or an invisible or underground, rather female supernatural being of Norrland belief, comparable to the skogsrå or elves (älvor).
claims.statement_id: Vittra atau vitter adalah bentuk sampingan dari vätte dan merujuk bangsa mitis dalam kepercayaan budaya fäbod Nordik utara, atau makhluk gaib tak kasatmata atau bawah tanah yang lebih sering perempuan dalam kepercayaan Norrland, sebanding dengan skogsrå atau peri (älvor).
claims.quote: Vittra eller vitter är en sidoform till vätte (vätter) och avser ett mytiskt folk inom den norra nordiska fäbodkulturens folktro, ibland särskilt som vitterfolk, eller ett övernaturligt osynligt eller underjordiskt snarare kvinnligt väsen i norrländsk folktro, jämförbart med skogsrå eller älvor

claims.statement: The southern limit of vittra belief runs roughly through Hälsingland and Dalarna, and it exists in Norway (Norge) and Finland too; vittra legends recall the Norwegian huldrefolk and the Gutnish tales of di sma undar jordi.
claims.statement_id: Batas selatan kepercayaan vittra kira-kira melintasi Hälsingland dan Dalarna, dan juga ada di Norwegia (Norge) dan Finlandia (Finland); legenda vittra mengingatkan pada kisah huldrefolk di Norwegia dan kisah Gotland tentang di sma undar jordi.
claims.quote: Sydgränsen för vittertron går ungefär genom Hälsingland och Dalarna, och finns även i Norge och Finland. Sägnerna om vittra påminner om de i Norge förekommande om huldrefolket, och gutniska berättelser om di sma undar jordi.

claims.statement: The vittra stay on the summer pasture (fäbodvallen) in winter when people are absent, and keep their own cattle called vitterkor, considered especially enchanted.
claims.statement_id: Vittra tinggal di padang penggembalaan (fäbodvallen) pada musim dingin ketika manusia tak ada, dan memelihara ternak sendiri yang disebut vitterkor, sapi yang dianggap sangat bertuah.
claims.quote: De håller till på fäbodvallen under vinterhalvåret då människorna inte är där. Vittra sägs hålla egen boskap, som kallas vitterkor, och dessa kor ansågs som särskilt förtrollade.

claims.statement: The vittra's paths are called vitterstråk, and many places have old maps of them; woe to whoever builds a house right on a vitterstråk, for the vittra will walk their cattle straight through it.
claims.statement_id: Jalur vittra disebut vitterstråk, dan di banyak tempat ada peta lamanya; celakalah yang membangun rumah tepat di atas vitterstråk, sebab vittra akan berjalan dengan ternaknya menembus rumah itu.
claims.quote: Vittras vägar kallas för vitterstråk, och på många platser finns det kartor över dessa från förr. Illa går det för den som bygger sitt hus rakt på ett vitterstråk, då går vittra med sin boskap tvärs genom huset.

claims.statement: The word vittra is etymologically related to vätte, used south of Dalarna, and comes from Old Norse (fornnordiskt) vættr, '(supernatural) being'.
claims.statement_id: Kata vittra berkerabat secara etimologis dengan vätte, yang dipakai di selatan Dalarna, dan berasal dari Nordik Kuno (fornnordiskt) vættr, "makhluk (gaib)".
claims.quote: Ordet "vittra" är etymologiskt besläktat med "vätte", som används söder om Dalarna. Det kommer från ett fornnordiskt vættr, vilket helt enkelt betyder "(övernaturligt) väsen".

description.en: Vritra (Sanskrit: वृत्र, lit. 'enveloper', IAST: Vṛtrá, Vedic Sanskrit pronunciation: [ʋr̩.trɐ́]) is a danava in Hinduism. He serves as the personification of drought, and is an adversary of the king of the devas, Indra. As a danava, he belongs to the race of the asuras. Vritra is also known in the Vedas as Ahi (Sanskrit: अहि, lit. 'snake' IAST: ahi Sanskrit pronunciation: [ɐ.hi]). He appears as a human-like serpent blocking the course of the Rigvedic rivers, and is slain by Indra with his newly forged vajra.

The Indo-Iranian word is also found in Avestan as vərəθraγna (Vedic vṛtraghná), literally "(one who) slays obstacles".

description.en: Waitoreke, also commonly referred to as the South Island otter, is an otter/beaver-like creature in New Zealand folklore. In its rare inferred sightings it is usually described as a small otter-like animal that lives in the South Island of New Zealand. There are many theories on the waitoreke's true identity, such as it being an otter, beaver or pinniped. New Zealand's only recognised endemic land mammals are bats—New Zealand lesser short-tailed bat and New Zealand long-tailed bat. Land mammals introduced to New Zealand by the seafaring Polynesian ancestors of Maori, apparent to the early European visitors and settlers, were kurī (dog) and kiore (rat).

description.en: Watatsumi (海神; 綿津見) [watatsɯmi], also pronounced Wadatsumi, is a kami (神, god; deity; spirit), Japanese dragon and tutelary water deity in Japanese mythology. Ōwatatsumi no kami (大綿津見神; "great deity of the sea") is believed to be another name for the sea deity Ryūjin (龍神, Dragon God) and also for the Watatsumi Sanjin (綿津見三神; "Three Watatsumi gods"), which rule the upper, middle and lower seas respectively and were created when Izanagi was washing himself of the dragons blood when he returned from Yomi, "the underworld". The main shrine is Shikaumi Shrine on Shika Island in Fukuoka Prefecture.

description.en: The Wawel Dragon (Polish: Smok Wawelski), also known as the Dragon of Wawel Hill, is a famous dragon in Polish legend. According to the earliest account (13th century), a dragon (holophagos, "one who swallows whole") plagued the capital city of Kraków established by legendary King Krak (or Krakus, Gracchus, etc.). The man-eating monster was being appeased with a weekly ration of cattle, until finally being defeated by the king's sons using decoy cows stuffed with sulfur. But the younger prince ("Krak the younger" or "Krak junior") murdered his elder brother to take sole credit, and was banished afterwards. Consequently Princess Wanda had to succeed the kingdom. Later in a 15th-century chronicle, the prince-names were swapped, with the elder as "Krak junior" and the younger as Lech. It also credited the king himself with masterminding the carcasses full of sulfur and other reagents. A yet later chronicler (Marcin Bielski, 1597) credited the stratagem to a cobbler named Skub (Skuba), adding that the "Dragon's Cave" (Polish: Smocza Jama) lay beneath Wawel Castle (on Wawel Hill on the bank of the Vistula River).

description.id: Naga Wales (bahasa Wales: y Ddraig Goch, berarti 'sang naga merah'; diucapkan [ə ˈðraiɡ ˈɡoːχ]) adalah simbol heraldik yang muncul pada bendera nasional Wales. Penggunaan naga tertua yang tercatat untuk melambangkan Wales adalah dalam Historia Brittonum, yang ditulis sekitar tahun 829 M, tetapi secara populer dianggap sebagai standar pertempuran Raja Arthur dan para pemimpin Celtic kuno lainnya. Hubungannya dengan para pemimpin ini, bersama dengan bukti lain dari arkeologi, sastra, dan sejarah dokumenter, membuat banyak orang mengira bahwa itu berevolusi dari simbol nasional Romawi-Inggris sebelumnya. Selama pemerintahan raja Tudor (mereka sendiri berasal dari Welsh), naga merah digunakan sebagai pendukung dalam lambang Kerajaan Inggris. Naga merah sering dianggap melambangkan segala hal Welsh, dan digunakan oleh banyak institusi publik dan swasta. Ini termasuk Pemerintah Welsh, Senedd, Visit Wales, banyak otoritas lokal termasuk Blaenau Gwent, Cardiff, Carmarthenshire, Rhondda Cynon Taf, dan Swansea, dan badan olahraga termasuk Asosiasi Sepak Bola Wales, Wrexham AFC, Newport Gwent Dragons, dan London Welsh RFC, sedangkan "lidah naga" (Tafod y Ddraig) adalah simbol dari Masyarakat Bahasa Welsh. Naga Welsh juga merupakan salah satu Binatang Ratu.
description.en: The Welsh Dragon (Welsh: y Ddraig Goch, meaning 'the red dragon', pronounced [ə ˈðraiɡ ˈɡoːχ]) is a heraldic symbol that represents Wales and appears on the national flag of Wales. Ancient leaders of the Celtic Britons that are personified as dragons include Maelgwn Gwynedd, Mynyddog Mwynfawr and Urien Rheged. Later Welsh "dragons" include Owain Gwynedd, Llywelyn ap Gruffydd and Owain Glyndŵr. The red dragon appears in the ancient Mabinogion story of Lludd and Llefelys where it is confined, battling with an invading white dragon, at Dinas Emrys. The story continues in the Historia Brittonum, written around AD 829, where Gwrtheyrn, King of the Britons is frustrated in attempts to build a fort at Dinas Emrys. He is told by a boy, Emrys, to dig up two dragons fighting beneath the castle. He discovers the white dragon representing the Anglo-Saxons, which is soon to be defeated by the red dragon of Wales. The red dragon is now seen as symbolising Wales, present on the current national flag of Wales, which became an official flag in 1959.

description.en: In Slavic mythology, a werewolf is a human-shapeshifter who temporarily takes the form of a wolf. Werewolves were often described as ordinary wolves, though some accounts noted peculiarities in appearance or behavior that hinted at their human origin. Werewolves retain human intelligence but cannot speak. According to folk beliefs, transformation into a wolf is the most common form of shapeshifting among Slavs. The concept is ancient and appears to varying degrees among all Slavic peoples, with the most detailed accounts among Belarusians, Poles, and Ukrainians. In Russian folklore, the character is often simply called a shapeshifter, sharing clear similarities with the werewolf. South Slavic traditions sometimes conflate werewolves with vampires. It was believed that sorcerers could transform into wolves by reciting spells and performing actions such as leaping, stepping over, tumbling through, or passing through magically imbued objects, or draping them over themselves. To revert to human form, sorcerers typically needed to repeat the actions in reverse. Sorcerers voluntarily became werewolves to cause harm to others. Some beliefs described people born with a predisposition to periodic shapeshifting due to their parents' actions or as punishment for their own sins. Such werewolves were thought to exhibit zoomorphic traits in human form, such as hair resembling wolf fur. Transformations often occurred at night or during specific seasons. These werewolves were believed to lack control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even humans, including loved ones, and were sometimes associated with cannibalism. Ancient beliefs linked werewolves to celestial events like eclipses. Folk beliefs also held that sorcerers or witches could transform a person into a wolf, often as an act of revenge, by casting spells on a wolf skin, belt, or enchanted door, among other methods. A popular narrative involved transforming an entire wedding party into wolves. The duration of the transformation ranged from days to years. Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longing for human life and avoiding true wolves. They were thought to avoid carrion and raw meat, subsisting on foraged food or stolen human provisions. Numerous methods were described to restore their human form. Werewolf beliefs incorporated much of the wolf's symbolism in Slavic culture. The myth likely originated from ancient totemic beliefs and rites of youthful initiation. The werewolf image may have been influenced by observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old and sick wolves. The concept has been reflected in Slavic literature.

description.en: In Arkansas folklore, the White River Monster is a large creature reportedly first spotted off the banks of the White River near Newport in northeastern Arkansas. Although reported in the press as a "monster", it is reported to be deeply loved by neighborhood residents near this portion of the White River, and the monster is referred to locally as "Whitey".

description.en: Wihwin is the name given to a malevolent water spirit of Central America, particularly associated with the Miskito tribe. Similar mythological creatures around the world include the kelpie in Scotland, the Scandinavian bäckahäst and the Australian bunyip. Although normally a sea-dwelling demon, it prowls through mountain ridges during the summer months. The horse-shaped monster has "jaws fenced round with horrid teeth", which it uses to consume humans and other prey it finds on its nocturnal hunts.

description.en: The Women in Black of Wat Samian Nari is a Thai urban legend that revolves around the ghosts of two women dressed in black, who are said to appear near the front of Wat Samian Nari in Bangkok late at night. It is considered one of the most famous contemporary urban legends of Bangkok.

description.en: Xelhua is one of the seven giants in Aztec mythology who escaped the flood by ascending the mountain of Tlaloc in the terrestrial paradise and afterwards built the Great Pyramid of Cholula. One of the six giants sons of Mixcoatl, the personification of the Milky Way:Surrounded the Earth by the seas and submerged in them for a long time, the old frog, with a thousand jaws and bloody tongues, and the strange name it takes, Tlaltecuhtli; Iztac-Mixcoatl, the fierce white cloud serpent, who lives in Citlalco, joins her in sweet collusion. And six tlacame with love engender; the six brothers on earth dwell and are the trunk of various races: the first-born, the giant Xelhua, of Itzocan and Epatlan, and Cuauquechollan, the cities he founded. Tenoch, the great Aztec claudillo, in Mexico stops the march of his people, and builds the great Tenochtitlan, a lake city. The strong Cuetlachoapan founds Ulmecatl, and gives its indolent people a seat. On the shores of the gulf, Xicalancatl, the brave Mixtecatl takes refuge. Of Mixtecapan in the sour lands; Otomitl, the xocoyotl [younger son], always lives in mountains near Mexico, and there it thrives in rich populations such as Tollan, Xilotepec and Otompan

description.id: Xiezhi (獬豸) adalah binatang dalam mitologi Tiongkok dan Korea yang dijuluki Anjing Pemakan Api. Xiezhi yang memakan api dijadikan sebagai lambang pelindung dari api dan kebakaran. Di Korea, patung dan gambar xiezhi banyak terdapat di bangunan-bangunan kuno berarsitektur kayu. Di Korea, hewan ini disebut haetae (해태). Xiezhi adalah hewan yang dapat membedakan mana benar atau salah, baik atau jahat. Selain itu, xiezhi juga memiliki tanduk. Apabila ia melihat pertengkaran atau perselisihan, tanduknya akan ia arahkan ke pihak yang berbuat salah. Ia selalu jujur bahkan jika pihak yang bersalah adalah kaisar. Dalam buku tentang pakaian istana dari Dinasti Han tertulis "Topi Keadilan dibuat untuk mereka yang menjalankan hukum negara, dan Topi Xiezhi adalah topi yang melambangkan keadilan". Pada zaman Dinasti Qing, peraturan mewajibkan para penulis resmi, komisaris pengawas dan inspektur polisi memakai seragam yang dilengkapi sulaman berpola xiezhi guna mengingatkan mereka agar bekerja dengan adil dan jujur. Puyi, kaisar Cina yang terakhir, menyebutkan bahwa ia memiliki patung xiezhi di depan meja kerjanya sebagai pengingat bahwa ia harus adil dalam memerintah.
description.en: The xiezhi (獬豸; xièzhì < Eastern Han Chinese *gɛʔ-ḍɛʔ) is a mythical creature of Chinese origin found throughout Sinospheric legends. It resembles an ox or goat, with thick dark fur covering its body, bright eyes and a single long horn on its forehead. It has great intellect and understands human speech. The xiezhi possesses the innate ability to distinguish right from wrong and when it finds corrupt officials, it will ram them with its horn and devour them. It is known as a symbol of justice.

description.en: Yacumama (from Quechua for "mother of water"), is a mythical enormous serpent believed to inhabit the Amazon Rainforest. According to legend, it is considered the mother of all aquatic animals and would suck up any living thing that passed within 100 steps of it. To protect themselves, local Indigenous peoples would blow on a conch horn before entering the water, believing that the Yacumama would reveal itself if it were present.

description.en: The term yamabito (山人) or sanjin, as understood in Japanese folklore, has come to be applied to a group, some scholars claim, of ancient, marginalized people, dating back to some unknown date during the Jōmon period of the history of Japan. The term itself has been translated as "mountain people", or as Dickins interprets the word as "woodsman", but there is more to it than that. It is from texts recorded by historian Kunio Yanagita that introduced, through their legends and tales, of the concept of being spirited away into Japanese popular culture.

description.en: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a legendary vampiric monster found in Southeastern Australian Aboriginal mythology. The legend is recounted by David Unaipon. According to legend, the creature resembles a little red frog-like man with a very big head, a large mouth with no teeth and suckers on the ends of its hands and feet. The Yara-ma-yha-who is said to live in fig trees. Instead of hunting for food, it is described as waiting for an unsuspecting traveller to rest under the tree. The creature then drops down and uses its suckers to drain the victim's blood. After that, it swallows the person, drinks some water, and then takes a nap. When the Yara-ma-yha-who awakens, it regurgitates the victim, leaving them shorter than before. The victim's skin also has a reddish tint that it did not have before. If this process is repeated, the victim becomes a Yara-ma-yha-who themselves. According to legend, the Yara-ma-yha-who is only active during the day and only targets living prey. "Playing dead" until sunset is offered as a ploy to avoid attack. Additionally, the folklore said that the Yara-ma-yha-who was not meant to be seen and got rid of anybody who glimpsed it. Stories of this creature were reportedly told to misbehaving children. The origin of this creature is believed to be the tarsier; it is probable that the story was brought to Australia by Malay settlers. The other theory proposed is Thylacoleo carnifex, a carnivorous marsupial that dropped onto its prey from the tree tops, which fits Yara-ma-yha-who dropping from fig trees onto its victims.

description.id: Naga Kuning (Hanzi Tradisional: 黃龍; Hanzi Sederhana: 黄龙; Pinyin: Huánglóng; Alih aksara Yale: Wong4 Lung4; bahasa Jepang: [[Kōryū or Ōryū] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan); bahasa Korea: [[Hwang-Ryong] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan); bahasa Vietnam: Hoàng Long) adalah titisan Dewa Kuning berwujud hewan, pusat alam semesta dalam kepercayaan tradisional Tionghoa dan mitologi Tiongkok. Kaisar Kuning atau Dewa Kuning dikandung oleh seorang ibu perawan, Fubao, yang menjadi hamil setelah melihat sinar cahaya kuning yang berputar di sekitar Biduk Utara (dalam teologi Tionghoa simbol utama Tuhan). Dua puluh empat bulan kemudian, Kaisar Kuning lahir dan dikaitkan dengan warna kuning karena merupakan warna Bumi (Dì 地), substansi material di mana dia menitis.
description.en: The Yellow Dragon (simplified Chinese: 黄龙; traditional Chinese: 黃龍; pinyin: Huánglóng; Cantonese Yale: Wong4 Lung4) is the zoomorphic incarnation of the Yellow Emperor of the center of the universe in Chinese religion and mythology. The Yellow Emperor or Yellow Deity was conceived by Fubao, who became pregnant after seeing a yellow ray of light turning around the Northern Dipper (in Chinese theology the principal symbol of God). Twenty-four months later, the Yellow Emperor was born and was associated with the color yellow because it is the color of the earth (地; Dì), the material substance in which he incarnated. The Yellow Dragon is a part of Wuxing and the Four Symbols as the embodiment of the element of earth.

description.id: Yōkai (妖怪) adalah kelas obake, makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Jepang (dengan banyak asal dari Tiongkok) yang terdiri dari setan oni sampai kitsune atau wanita salju Yuki-onna. description.en: Yōkai (妖怪; Japanese pronunciation: [joː.kai]) are a class of supernatural entities and spirits in Japanese folklore. Yōkai are a vast range of beings, including shapeshifters, ghosts, demons, and tricksters. They can be mischievous, helpful, or malevolent, often appearing as animal-like figures, possessed objects, or humanoids. They embody the mysterious and uncanny aspects of nature and human emotions. Yōkai are also referred to as ayakashi (あやかし), mononoke (物の怪) or mamono (魔物). Some academics and Shinto practitioners acknowledge similarities within the seeming dichotomy between the natures of yōkai and most kami, which are generally regarded as relatively beneficent in comparison, and class the two as ultimately the same type of spirits of nature or of a mythological realm. Their behavior can range from malevolent or mischievous to benevolent towards humans. Yōkai often have animal-like features (such as the kappa, depicted as appearing similar to a turtle, and the tengu, commonly depicted with wings), but may also appear humanoid in appearance, such as the kuchisake-onna (口裂け女). Some yōkai resemble inanimate objects (such as the tsukumogami), while others have no discernible shape. Yōkai are typically described as having spiritual or supernatural abilities, with shapeshifting being the most common trait associated with them. Yōkai that shapeshift are known as bakemono (化け物) or obake (お化け). Japanese folklorists and historians, such as Michael Foster, describe yōkai as part of how humans "fashion from a perilous landscape something concrete [...] the naming of yōkai identifies the threat, specifying the nature of the danger..." In the Edo period (1603 to 1868), many artists, such as Toriyama Sekien (1712-1788), invented new yōkai by taking inspiration from folktales or purely from their imagination. Today, several such yōkai (such as the amikiri) are mistakenly thought to originate in more traditional folklore. The kanji representation of the word yōkai comprises two characters that both mean "suspicious, doubtful", and while the Japanese name is simply the Japanese transliteration or pronunciation of the Chinese term yāoguài (which designates similarly strange creatures), some Japanese commentators argue that the word yōkai has taken on many different meanings in Japanese culture, including referring to a large number of uniquely Japanese creatures.

description.en: The Ypotryll is a Medieval European chimeric creature featured in heraldry. It has the tusked head of a wild boar or hog, the humped body of a camel, the legs and hooves of an ox or goat and the long, scaly tail of a serpent. Its name is thought to be derived from the Greek hippo (horse), or in Middle English ypotame, itself derived from the Latin ypotamus. Little is known of the creature's meanings or origins, but it appears as the badge of John Tiptoft, 1st Earl of Worcester, also known as the "Butcher of England"; a man known for his extreme cruelty in regards to the execution of Lancastrians during his rule as Lord High Constable in the early 1460s. Tiptoft was beheaded in 1470 by the Lancastrians during the War of the Roses (1455–1487).

claims.statement_id: Tiptoft dipenggal kaum Lancaster pada 1470 dalam Perang Mawar.
claims.quote: Tiptoft was beheaded in 1470 by the Lancastrians during the War of the Roses

description.id: Yuki-onna (雪女, secara harfiah berarti "Wanita Salju") adalah sosok spirit atau yōkai dalam cerita rakyat Jepang. Ia merupakan figur populer dalam sastra Jepang, manga, dan anime. Kadang kala ia juga disebut sebagai Gadis Salju (雪娘, Yuki-musume), Peri Salju (yuki-onago), Sundal Salju (yukijorō), Kakak Salju (yuki anesa), Ibu Salju (yuki-omba), Nenek Salju (yukinba; dari Ehime）, yukifuri-baba (dari Nagano).
description.en: Yuki-onna (雪女; lit. 'snow woman') is a yūrei or yōkai in Japanese folklore that is often depicted in Japanese literature, films, or animation. She may also go by such names as yuki-musume (雪娘, "snow daughter"), yukihime (雪姫, "snow princess"), yuki-onago (雪女子, "snow girl"), yukijorō (雪女郎, "snow woman"), yuki anesa (雪姉さ, "snow sis"), yuki-onba (雪乳母, "snow granny" or "snow nanny"), yukinba (雪婆, "snow hag") in Ehime, yukifuri-baba (雪降り婆々, "snowfall witch" or "snowfall hag") in Nagano. They are also called several names that are related to icicles, such as tsurara-onna, kanekori-musume, and shigama-nyōbō.

claims.statement: Yuki-onna is a Japanese yōkai without a single definitive story.
claims.statement_id: Yuki-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang tidak mempunyai satu kisah tunggal.
claims.quote: The Yuki Onna is one of Japan’s most well-known and yet unknown yokai. There is no single story of the Yuki Onna.

claims.statement: The name Yuki-onna means snow woman.
claims.statement_id: Nama Yuki-onna berarti perempuan salju.
claims.quote: Yuki Onna uses the kanji 雪 (yuki; snow) + 女 (onna; woman) to mean Snow Woman.

claims.statement: Yuki-onna stories occur in snowy parts of Japan and have regional variants.
claims.statement_id: Cerita Yuki-onna terdapat di daerah Jepang yang bersalju dan memiliki variasi daerah.
claims.quote: Anywhere there is ice and snow in Japan you will find legends of the Yuki Onna, often called by some regional variation.

claims.statement: Yuki-onna is often depicted with white skin and a white kimono.
claims.statement_id: Yuki-onna kerap digambarkan berkulit putih dan mengenakan kimono putih.
claims.quote: She resembles a classic yurei, with snow-white skin and a white kimono. The kimono is usually described as a thin, summer kimono

claims.statement: In Hearn’s story, a woman in white blows her breath on Mosaku.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Hearn, seorang perempuan berbaju putih meniupkan napasnya ke Mosaku.
claims.quote: he saw a woman in the room,—a woman all in white. She was bending above Mosaku, and blowing her breath upon him

claims.statement: The woman spares Minokichi because he is young.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu membiarkan Minokichi hidup karena usianya muda.
claims.quote: But I cannot help feeling some pity for you,—because you are so young... You are a pretty boy, Minokichi; and I will not hurt you now.

claims.statement: The woman forbids Minokichi from telling anyone and threatens to kill him if he does.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu melarang Minokichi bercerita kepada siapa pun dan mengancam akan membunuhnya jika ia melanggar.
claims.quote: But, if you ever tell anybody—even your own mother—about what you have seen this night, I shall know it; and then I will kill you

claims.statement: O-Yuki reveals she was the snow woman Minokichi met.
claims.statement_id: O-Yuki mengaku sebagai perempuan salju yang ditemui Minokichi.
claims.quote: “It was I—I—I! Yuki it was! And I told you then that I would kill you if you ever said one word about it!

description.id: Yūrei (幽霊) adalah figur dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, yang sepadan dengan hantu. Istilah tersebut terdiri dari dua huruf kanji, 幽 (yū), berarti "redup" atau "samar", dan 霊 (rei), berarti "jiwa" atau "spirit." Nama alternatifnya antara lain Bōrei (亡霊) yang berarti arwah orang meninggal, Shiryō (死霊) berarti jiwa orang mati, atau dalam pengertian yang lebih luas meliputi Yōkai (妖怪) atau Obake (お化け). Seperti padanan mereka dalam mitologi Tionghoa dan Barat, mereka diyakini sebagai jiwa setelah mati.
description.en: Yūrei (幽霊) are figures in Japanese folklore analogous to the Western concept of ghosts. The name consists of two kanji, 幽 (yū), meaning "faint" or "dim" and 霊 (rei), meaning "soul" or "spirit". Alternative names include Bōrei (亡霊), meaning ruined or departed spirit, Shiryō (死霊), meaning dead spirit, or the more encompassing Yōkai (妖怪) or Obake (お化け). Like their Western counterparts, they are thought to be spirits barred from a peaceful afterlife.

claims.statement: Yūrei is the spirit of a deceased person.
claims.statement_id: Yūrei adalah roh seseorang yang sudah meninggal.
claims.quote: Generally speaking, a yūrei is the spirit of a person who has died, usually appearing as they did in life.

claims.statement: The meaning of the Japanese word yūrei changed over the centuries.
claims.statement_id: Makna kata yūrei dalam bahasa Jepang berubah selama berabad-abad.
claims.quote: The Japanese word yūrei conjures up an image today of a spiteful ghost, but its meaning has changed considerably over the centuries.

claims.statement: Yūrei may remain in the human world for personal reasons or insufficient funeral rites.
claims.statement_id: Yūrei dapat tinggal di dunia manusia karena alasan pribadi atau upacara pemakaman yang kurang memadai.
claims.quote: Yūrei refers to the spirits of humans who do not cross over to the other side and remain in the human world for personal reasons or because the funeral or burial rites were not sufficient or satisfactory.

claims.statement: In art and literature yūrei are often shown as long-haired women in burial clothes, with dangling hands and no feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni dan sastra, yūrei lazim digambarkan sebagai perempuan berambut hitam panjang, berpakaian pemakaman, bertangan menggantung, dan tanpa kaki.
claims.quote: The typical yūrei, as depicted in art and literature, is described as a woman with long, disheveled black hair obstructing the face, wearing burial clothing, with curved dangling hands and no feet.

claims.statement: In ancient and medieval Japan, yūrei usually meant souls of the dead who neither appeared nor cursed.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang kuno dan pertengahan, yūrei biasanya berarti jiwa orang mati yang tidak menampakkan diri atau mengutuk.
claims.quote: In ancient and medieval Japan, when there was considerable “commerce” between the people of this world and spirits, the word yūrei typically referred to the souls of the dead, who neither showed themselves nor enacted curses.

claims.statement: Around the fifteenth century, yūrei began to mean resentful spirits.
claims.statement_id: Sekitar abad kelima belas, yūrei mulai berarti roh yang menyimpan dendam.
claims.quote: Around the fifteenth century, the word yūrei began to shift from describing the souls of the memorialized dead to represent spirits harboring a grudge.

claims.statement: In the Edo period, people believed a bad relationship in life could lead to revenge after death.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman Edo, hubungan buruk semasa hidup dipercaya dapat berujung pada pembalasan setelah kematian.
claims.quote: In the Edo period (1603–1868), there was a belief that a bad relationship with someone in life could lead to that person taking revenge after death.

claims.statement: In the later Edo period, yūrei appeared in kabuki and inspired ukiyo-e artists.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir zaman Edo, yūrei kerap muncul dalam kabuki dan mengilhami seniman ukiyo-e.
claims.quote: In the later Edo period, it was common for yūrei to appear in kabuki, providing inspiration for ukiyo-e artists.

claims.statement: In the Edo period, ghost stories became popular and artists painted yūrei.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman Edo, cerita hantu menjadi populer dan seniman melukis yūrei.
claims.quote: there was a craze for kaidan (ghost stories) and many artists painted pictures of yūrei.

description.en: Zana (Zanë in Gheg or Zërë in Tosk, pl. zanë(t), see other variants below) is a nymph-like figure in Albanian mythology and folklore, usually associated with mountains, springs and streams, forests, vegetation and animals, human vital energy and sometimes destiny. Zana e Madhe ("the Great Zana") is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess, equivalent of the Ancient Greek Artemis and Roman Diana. The zana are considered in folk beliefs to be extraordinary courageous (thus the Albanian expression trim si zana) and they confer their protection on warriors similarly to Pallas Athena of Ancient Greece. Innumerable Albanian folk poems, myths and legends that are dedicated to Zana and her friends have been handed down to modern times. The zana are thought to have observed the speeches at the League of Prizren at 1878. Similar Albanian mythological figures with nymph-like attributes are: Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira and Fatí.

claims.statement: The zana (Gheg Zanë, Tosk Zërë) is a nymph-like figure of Albanian mythology tied to mountains, springs, streams, forests, plants, animals, human vital energy and sometimes destiny; Zana e Madhe ("the Great Zana") is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess equivalent to the Greek Artemis and Roman Diana.
claims.statement_id: Zana (Zanë dalam Gheg, Zërë dalam Tosk) adalah sosok mirip nimfa dalam mitologi Albania yang terkait gunung, mata air, sungai, hutan, tumbuhan, hewan, energi hidup manusia, dan kadang takdir; Zana e Madhe ("Zana Agung") diduga dewi Iliria setara Artemis Yunani dan Diana Romawi.
claims.quote: is a nymph-like figure in Albanian mythology and folklore, usually associated with mountains, springs and streams, forests, vegetation and animals, human vital energy and sometimes destiny. Zana e Madhe ("the Great Zana") is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess, equivalent of the Ancient Greek Artemis and Roman Diana.

claims.statement: Folk belief considers the zana extraordinarily courageous (hence the Albanian expression trim si zana), and they protect warriors like Pallas Athena of Ancient Greece.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat zana dianggap luar biasa berani (sehingga ada ungkapan Albania trim si zana) dan melindungi para pejuang seperti Pallas Athena dari Yunani Kuno.
claims.quote: The zana are considered in folk beliefs to be extraordinary courageous (thus the Albanian expression trim si zana) and they confer their protection on warriors similarly to Pallas Athena of Ancient Greece.

claims.statement: The Illyrian Thana (a nymph, fairy or deity named in Roman-era votive inscriptions) is traditionally considered the precursor of the Albanian Zana and a cognate of Latin Diāna.
claims.statement_id: Thana dari Iliria (nama nimfa, peri, atau dewa dalam prasasti nazar zaman Romawi) secara tradisional dianggap cikal bakal Zana Albania, dan dipandang seasal dengan Diāna dalam bahasa Latin.
claims.quote: the Illyrian Thana (the name of a nymph, fairy or deity, attested in votive inscriptions of the Roman era) is traditionally considered the precursor of the Albanian Zana. The theonym is also regarded as a cognate and equivalent of the Latin Diāna.

claims.statement: In Northern Albania and Kosovo every mountain is said to have its own zana, appearing as a fair maiden bathing in mountain streams; the original zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.
claims.statement_id: Di Albania utara dan Kosovo setiap gunung dikatakan punya zana sendiri, yang tampak sebagai gadis cantik mandi di sungai gunung; zana asli dikawal tiga kambing liar bertanduk emas.
claims.quote: In Northern Albania and Kosovo every mountain is said to have its own zana, who appeared as a fair maiden found bathing naked in mountain streams.

claims.statement: The zana is believed to have the power to petrify humans with a glance.
claims.statement_id: Zana dipercaya memiliki kekuatan membuat manusia membatu dengan tatapannya.
claims.quote: The zana is believed to have the power to petrify humans with a glance

claims.statement: Similar Albanian nymph-like figures are Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira and Fatí.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh mitologi Albania serupa yang mirip nimfa adalah Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira, dan Fatí.
claims.quote: Similar Albanian mythological figures with nymph-like attributes are: Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira and Fatí.

claims.statement: In Albanian folklore the original Zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Albania, Zana asli dikawal tiga kambing liar bertanduk emas.
claims.quote: In Albanian folklore the original Zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.

claims.statement: The zanas are thought to have watched the speeches at the League of Prizren in 1878.
claims.statement_id: Para zana dipercaya menyaksikan pidato-pidato di Liga Prizren tahun 1878.
claims.quote: Zanat mendohet se kanë vëzhguar fjalimet në Lidhjen e Prizrenit të vitit 1878.

description.en: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王; lit. "goodness-like dragon-king" or "goodness woman dragon-king", respectively) is a rain-god dragon in Japanese mythology. According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made Zennyo Ryūō appear in 824 AD during a famous rainmaking contest at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.

claims.statement: Zennyo Ryūō is a rain-associated dragon deity in Japanese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Zennyo Ryūō adalah dewa naga yang berkaitan dengan hujan dalam mitologi Jepang.
claims.quote: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王; lit. "goodness-like dragon-king" or "goodness woman dragon-king", respectively) is a rain-god dragon in Japanese mythology.

claims.statement: A Buddhist tradition links the dragon with Kūkai’s rainmaking rite in 824.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Buddha menghubungkan naga ini dengan ritual pemanggilan hujan oleh Kūkai pada 824.
claims.quote: According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made Zennyo Ryūō appear in 824 AD during a famous rainmaking contest at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.

claims.statement: The name includes an expression meaning dragon king.
claims.statement_id: Namanya memuat ungkapan yang berarti raja naga.
claims.quote: The dragon name Zennyo Ryūō is written in Japanese as 善 zen "good, goodness; virtuous", 女 nyo "woman; female" or 如 nyo "like; as if; be like; thus" (differentiated with the "mouth radical" 口), and 龍王 ryūō or 竜王 "dragon king".

claims.statement: Art represents the deity as a small dragon or as a human with a dragon’s tail.
claims.statement_id: Karya seni menggambarkannya sebagai naga kecil atau manusia berekor naga.
claims.quote: Zennyo is a common theme in Japanese art, usually depicted as a small dragon but sometimes as a human, either male or female, with a dragon's tail.

description.en: Zilant (; Russian: Зилант [zʲɪˈɫant]; Tatar: җылан, cılan [ʑɯˈɫɑn] – lit. 'snake') is a legendary creature, something between a dragon and a wyvern in Tatar mythology. Since 1730, it has been the official symbol of Kazan, the capital city of the Republic of Tatarstan in Russia. This winged snake is mentioned in legends about the foundation of Kazan. It is often described as a legendary creature with the head of a dragon, the body of a bird, the legs of a chicken, the tail of a snake, the red wings of a bat or bird, black feathers and scaly black skin.

claims.statement: Zilant is a legendary creature between a dragon and a wyvern in Tatar mythology.
claims.statement_id: Zilant adalah makhluk legendaris di antara naga dan wyvern dalam mitologi Tatar.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature, something between a dragon and a wyvern in Tatar mythology.

claims.statement: Since 1730 Zilant has been the official symbol of Kazan, capital of the Republic of Tatarstan in Russia, and this winged snake appears in legends of Kazan's founding.
claims.statement_id: Sejak 1730 Zilant menjadi lambang resmi Kazan, ibu kota Republik Tatarstan di Rusia, dan ular bersayap ini disebut dalam legenda pendirian Kazan.
claims.quote: Since 1730, it has been the official symbol of Kazan, the capital city of the Republic of Tatarstan in Russia. This winged snake is mentioned in legends about the foundation of Kazan.

claims.statement: The Zilant is a fabulous winged snake with the forepart of a dragon, part of Tatar and Russian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Zilant adalah makhluk dongeng berupa ular bersayap dengan bagian depan seekor naga, bagian dari cerita rakyat Tatar dan Rusia.
claims.quote: ist als geflügelte Schlange mit dem Vorderteil eines Drachen ein Fabelwesen, das ein Teil der tatarischen und russischen Folklore ist.

claims.statement: The word Zilant transcribes Russian Зилант, itself from Tatar yılan, "snake".
claims.statement_id: Kata Zilant adalah transkripsi Inggris dari bahasa Rusia Зилант, yang berasal dari kata Tatar yılan, "ular".
claims.quote: The word Zilant is the English transcription of Russian Зилант, itself a rendering of Tatar yılan/елан

claims.statement: Tatars saw it as a repulsive creature like the European and Persian dragon; in Idel-Ural belief any snake that lives 100 years becomes an ajdaha.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tatar menganggapnya makhluk menjijikkan yang sepadan dengan naga Eropa dan Persia; menurut kepercayaan Idel-Ural, ular yang hidup 100 tahun berubah menjadi ajdaha.
claims.quote: Tatars regarded it as a repulsive creature, corresponding to European and Persian dragon. According to Idel-Ural beliefs, any snake that survives for 100 years turns into an ajdaha.

claims.statement: The Zilant differs from Aq Yılan ('White Snake'), the king of snakes.
claims.statement_id: Zilant berbeda dari Aq Yılan ("Ular Putih"), raja para ular.
claims.quote: The Zilant/Ajdaha differs from Aq Yılan ('White Snake'), which is the king of snakes.

claims.statement: Despite its bird-like posture, the Zilant differs from the basilisk in having a dragon's head, not a bird's.
claims.statement_id: Meski posturnya mirip burung, Zilant berbeda dari basilisk karena kepalanya kepala naga, bukan kepala burung.
claims.quote: Vom Basilisk unterscheidet er sich trotz seiner vogelähnlichen Haltung durch den Kopf, der ein Drachen- und kein Vogelkopf ist

description.en: The zouyu (Chinese: 騶虞; pinyin: zōu yú), also called zouwu (騶吾; zōu wú) or zouya (騶牙; zōu yá), is a legendary creature mentioned in old Chinese literature.

claims.statement: Zouyu is a legendary creature in old Chinese literature, also named zouwu or zouya.
claims.statement_id: Zouyu adalah makhluk legenda dalam sastra Tiongkok lama, juga dikenal sebagai zouwu atau zouya.
claims.quote: The zouyu (Chinese: 騶虞; pinyin: zōu yú), also called zouwu (騶吾; zōu wú) or zouya (騶牙; zōu yá), is a legendary creature mentioned in old Chinese literature.

claims.statement: Duyvendak questions interpreting a Classic of Poetry poem as a reference to the Zouyu animal.
claims.statement_id: Penafsiran syair Kitab Nyanyian sebagai rujukan hewan Zouyu dipertanyakan Duyvendak.
claims.quote: The earliest known appearance of the characters 騶虞 (zōu yú) is in the Book of Songs, but J.J.L. Duyvendak describes the interpretation of that little poem as referring to an animal of that name as "very doubtful".

claims.statement: Accounts describe it as a righteous animal appearing under a benevolent ruler.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menggambarkannya sebagai hewan baik yang muncul pada pemerintahan penguasa berbudi.
claims.quote: The zouyu appears in a number of later works, where it is described as a "righteous" animal that, similarly to a qilin, only appears during the rule of a benevolent and sincere monarch. It is said to be as fierce-looking as a tiger, but gentle and strictly vegetarian, and described in some books (already in Shuowen Jiezi) as a white tiger with black spots.

claims.statement: Zouyu appears fierce like a tiger but is gentle and strictly vegetarian.
claims.statement_id: Zouyu berwajah garang seperti harimau, tetapi lembut dan hanya memakan tumbuhan.
claims.quote: The zouyu appears in a number of later works, where it is described as a "righteous" animal that, similarly to a qilin, only appears during the rule of a benevolent and sincere monarch. It is said to be as fierce-looking as a tiger, but gentle and strictly vegetarian, and described in some books (already in Shuowen Jiezi) as a white tiger with black spots.

claims.statement: In 1404, Zhu Su sent a creature described as Zouyu to the Yongle Emperor.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1404, Zhu Su mengirim makhluk yang disebut Zouyu kepada Kaisar Yongle.
claims.quote: In 1404, during the reign of the Yongle Emperor, Prince Zhu Su, his relative from Kaifeng (in modern-day Henan province) sent him a captured zouyu spotted and captured in Shenhou

claims.statement: Some modern authors propose the giant panda as the animal identified as Zouyu.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penulis modern mengusulkan panda raksasa sebagai identifikasi hewan Zouyu.
claims.quote: Puzzled about the real zoological identity of the zouyu said to be captured during the Yongle era, Duyvendak exclaimed, "Can it possibly have been a Pandah?" Following him, some modern authors consider zouyu to refer to the giant panda.
